item.title: College football Week 10 players to watch: Can LSU's Sam Leavitt sustain his momentum after back-to-back games without a turnover?
item.description: Christmas is just under two months away, but College Football Christmas may come in Week 10. After the first 2026 CFP rankings on Tuesday, seven Saturday matchups now feature both teams ranked in the current Top 25. It's clear the committee is going to let this weekend solve some of the ranking scenarios, making the games that much more important and exciting. With some marquee matchups and a full slate of other games, here are our Week 10 players to watch. New Mexico safety Austin Brawley New Mexico at Nevada (Friday, 9 p.m. ET, CBSSN/DirecTV) Brawley has four interceptions this season for the Lobos. That is tied for the sixth-most in the FBS. The safety also has back-to-back games with a pick. Nevada quarterbacks have thrown 12 interceptions already this season. The Wolf Pack have featured four different QBs under center this year, but with those numbers it doesn't matter who they trot out. Brawley should have a good chance to come down with another INT this weekend. LSU QB Sam Leavitt No. 5 Alabama at No. 14 LSU (3:30 p.m. ET, ABC, DirecTV) Leavitt was one of the biggest transfer portal names to watch last offseason, and that only got bigger when he landed at LSU under new head coach Lane Kiffin. It looked like a perfect match in LSU's first game with a blowout win over the Clemson Tigers. The following week, he continued his hot start, throwing for 340 yards and rushing for three touchdowns. Leavitt threw three interceptions in that game against Louisiana Tech, though, and his ball security came into question. Leavitt had varying performances over his next few games, but one constant: He threw one interception in each game. The LSU quarterback has improved significantly over his last two games. Leavitt has completed 76% of his passes for 682 yards and seven touchdowns with no interceptions or fumbles lost in that span. On Saturday, he will face Alabama's defense, which forces 1.5 interceptions per game, tied for the fifth-best rate in the FBS. Sam Leavitt of the LSU Tigers passes the ball during a game against the Auburn Tigers on October 24, 2026. (Stew Milne/Getty Images) Stew Milne via Getty Images West Virginia QB Michael Hawkins Jr. West Virginia at No. 15 Texas Tech (9:30 p.m. ET, ESPN/DirecTV) Hawkins is listed as a quarterback, but he is having one of the better rushing seasons in the FBS. He has scored on the ground at least once in each game this season and has 16 rushing touchdowns, the second-most in the FBS. His 836 rushing yards rank 15th in the FBS, and third-most for a quarterback behind Navy's Jackson Gutierrez and Army's Cale Hellums. The biggest difference is that Navy and Army both run a triple-option offense that needs a mobile quarterback to succeed. West Virginia doesn't run that type of offense, making Hawkins' performance this year so far even more impressive. item.title: U17WWC: Tinubu urges Flamingos to stay focused ahead of the final
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Abuja President Bola Tinubu has congratulated Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, on their impressive victory over Brazil in Wednesday’s semi-final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The president described the team’s qualification for the final as a remarkable achievement that has brought immense pride and joy to millions of Nigerians at home and abroad. President Tinubu, in a statement by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, applauded the coaching crew and all those whose hard work and support contributed to the team’s successful campaign. As the Flamingos prepare to face Japan in the final, the President urges the players to remain focused, confident, and determined, assuring them of the prayers, goodwill, and unflinching support of the Nigerian nation. He said, “I encourage you to approach the final with the same fighting spirit and belief that have brought you this far. I have confidence in your ability to make history by winning the coveted world title. “I call on all Nigerians to rally behind the young ambassadors of the nation, whose achievements continue to showcase Nigeria’s sporting excellence and inspire a new generation of girls to pursue their dreams uninhibited. “Once again, Nigeria is proud of you. Go for the trophy, Flamingos!” he added. The post U17WWC: Tinubu urges Flamingos to stay focused ahead of the final appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Former F1 champion Jones dies aged 80
item.description: Jones helped turn Williams into one of the major forces in F1 [Getty Images] Alan Jones, the last Australian and first Williams driver to win the Formula 1 world title, has died at the age of 80. Jones raced in F1 between 1975 and 1986, winning the title in 1980 to become the first of Williams' seven world champions. Jones, who turned 80 on Monday, won 12 grands prix in his career and raced competitively in other formats until 2002. "We are extremely saddened to announce the passing of our beloved Alan, who passed away on 5 November following a short illness," his wife Amanda Butler-Davis said in a statement released on her behalf by Motorsport Australia. "He will be dearly missed and fondly remembered by those closest to him, as well as the many fans whose support he was always grateful for." Jones started the first of his 116 F1 races in a Hesketh at the 1975 Spanish Grand Prix. He won his first race for the Shadow team in Austria in 1977 before joining Williams the following year. After finishing third in the drivers' championship in 1979, he won five races in 1980 and finished on the podium in all but one of the grands prix he completed, taking the title ahead of Nelson Piquet. Jones was the second Australian to win the F1 championship, after Jack Brabham in 1959, 1960 and 1966. Jones remains the most recent Australian to triumph at the Australian Grand Prix, winning at Melbourne's Calder Park Raceway in 1980 when the race was not part of the world championship. He finished third in the drivers' standings in 1981, winning in Las Vegas for what proved to be his final race victory. He retired at the end of the season. Having appeared in one race for Arrows in 1983, Jones made a full-time comeback with new team Haas in 1985 and raced largely unsuccessfully the following year. He continued to compete in touring car and endurance races, mostly in Australia, and became a popular motorsports pundit on television in his home country. "Alan dedicated his life to motorsport, building a legacy that will live on through the countless people he touched along the way," Butler-Davis said. "Through his achievements, passion and unmistakable character, both on and off the track, Alan left an enduring mark on the sport both nationally and across the globe." Breaking new ground with Williams Jones, the Williams FW07 and Patrick Head and Frank Williams in Brazil in 1981 [Getty Images] Alan Jones' time at the very peak of F1 was short - essentially just under three years from mid-1979 to the end of 1981 - but he left a lasting impression. Jones is synonymous with the Williams team, having become their first world champion in 1980, and he formed a close, almost brotherly bond with co-founders Frank Williams and Patrick Head. Williams and Head loved Jones' pugnacious, no-nonsense approach, and between them they were the leading force in F1 for a short time, as the team first emerged at the forefront of the sport. item.title: Where to watch Miami Dolphins vs. Detroit Lions in Week 9
item.description: After beating the New York Jets in Week 7, the Miami Dolphins fell to the New England Patriots 24-19 last week at home, dropping to 1-6 on the season. Now, heading into Week 9, the Dolphins are set to take on the Detroit Lions at Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday afternoon. The 5-2 Lions have won their last three games, beating the Minnesota Vikings , Green Bay Packers and Arizona Cardinals . Ahead of this interconference battle, fans should take a look at this map to make sure they can catch the action on television. Those in the green areas will see Miami vs. Detroit, while those in red will see the New York Jets vs. Kansas City Chiefs, blue will see Carolina vs. Denver, yellow will see Cleveland vs. New Orleans and orange will get the Houston Texans vs. Los Angeles Chargers. The Dolphins and Lions will kick off at 1:00 p.m. ET, and the game will be broadcast on CBS. Kevin Harland will have the call with former NFL quarterback Trent Green providing color commentary and Melanie Collins reporting from the sidelines. item.title: Kyle Hamilton Q&A: All-Pro talks New Balance, Ravens defense, John Harbaugh, more | Exclusive
item.description: A lot has changed for the Baltimore Ravens in recent days. The emergency quarterback to start the season (and four days ago), Joe Fagnano , will start their Nov. 5 “Thursday Night Football” contest against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Quarterback Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery and landed him on injured reserve, meaning he’ll miss at least the next four games. His backup, Tyler Huntley , had his season end shortly after entering against the Buffalo Bills. Baltimore found its stopgap in veteran signal-caller Jacoby Brissett , whom they traded for Wednesday, Nov. 4. All of which made my interview with Ravens safety and two-time All-Pro Kyle Hamilton a bit outdated by the time he was ready to announce that he was joining New Balance as their newest addition to an athlete roster that includes Shohei Ohtani, Coco Gauff, Josh Allen and Cooper Flagg. Below you’ll find a condensed version of our conversation that still had plenty of interesting tidbits – from his relationship with first-year Ravens head coach Jesse Minter to his former coach John Harbaugh, that game-winning interception against the Atlanta Falcons, a concerning Ravens’ defensive trend and, of course, why he chose to partner with New Balance. (Questions and answers have been edited for length and clarity.) USA TODAY: So why New Balance? Kyle Hamilton: It’s been, this process of picking whichever company and everything, it’s been interesting. I think the moment I found out New Balance was interested, I think the interest was mutual. Being a family-owned company and talking to all the people there, it seemed a no-brainer. And I think my style fits with New Balance’s style. USAT: How would you describe Kyle Hamilton’s style? KH: First and foremost, I think it’s on brand for both brands – me and New Balance. I’m very athleisure, comfortable, I call it a “cozyfam” type of thing that I do. I don’t do a lot coming into games. Just sweatpants, sweatshirt, and I think that fits me pretty well with New Balance. USAT: Josh Allen is on New Balance’s roster, joining forces with him is kind of unique, a different dynamic for you I imagine? KH: Yeah, it’s a limited roster, obviously players like Josh, (Arizona Cardinals rookie running back) Jeremiyah Love, a Notre Dame guy, obviously a plethora of athletes in different sports as well, it’s pretty cool to be a part of. It’s a blessing. … Maybe we’ll have to talk about it on the field. USAT: Any product or line that you would like to have your input heard on immediately? KH: I’m still finding my way through the website. I’m trying to get as much stuff as I can first before I make decisions like that. But all the gear that I’ve gotten is amazing and they’ve done a great job with my family, getting them situated with a bunch of stuff. item.title: Beckett Hammers carries her family's Venice volleyball legacy forward
item.description: There are a lot of differences between the “old” gym and the new one. When Brook Hammers played at Venice in 1994, the gym was smaller and it had no air conditioning. Head coach Brian Wheatley, now a FHSAA Hall-of-Famer, was in his first season, leading an undecorated volleyball program. “It’s amazing because my 1994 team, the first year with Wheatley, was the first year that we ever won districts and regionals,” Hammers said. “So, I don’t want to say we started the tradition, but we kind of have.” Watch state volleyball games live in NFHS Network Now, 32 years later, Beckett Hammers — Brook’s daughter — is helping steward a new phase of Venice volleyball. The Indians have won the district title 25 consecutive times and 31 overall. They have won 13 regional championships, and they’re six-time state champions. Venice will look to add to their resume when they face Horizon on Friday, Nov. 6, at 11 a.m. in a Class 6A state semifinal in Winter Haven. But outside of a bigger, air-conditioned gym, Venice looks different in other ways. Wheatley left Venice in May 2024 after 30 seasons. For the first time in the state finals, the Indians will be led by head coach Jay Lanham, who has been coaching at Venice since 2003. The Elite 11: Who are Sarasota, Manatee's top volleyball players in 2026? And in their first state finals appearance since 2022, Beckett has been pivotal this season after moving to Florida last November. The junior outside hitter, who can play anywhere, has recorded a team-high 270 kills and 340 digs, 207 assists, 27 aces and 27 blocks. “She’s the type of kid who’s going to make the play,” Lanham said. “When you think that you need a big point, and you’re waiting on that huge swing, and she goes up hard and then she tips it, finds an open area on the court. That’s just a huge stop to their momentum…she’s our leader on the court.” “Since my mom graduated from Venice, I want to honor her name,” Beckett said. Brook laughs when she describes her Venice lineage. She’s “born and raised,” but that feels like an understatement. Her sister, Lori, played for Venice and coaches the freshman team. Her dad, Larry Sandburg, coached baseball and football before becoming a long-time athletic director from 1994 to 2008. Sandburg worked at Venice for 38 years. He helped hire the coaches that have turned Venice into the sports powerhouse it is, including baseball coach Craig Faulkner and football coaches John Peacock and Nick Coleman. Sandburg also hired Wheatley. The four have a combined 16 state championships. But for most of her life, Beckett has been over 600 miles away from those ties. Beckett played at Marvin Ridge High School in North Carolina, appearing in back-to-back state championship games as an underclassman under Brook, who was the head coach. Marvin Ridge lost in 2024, but won in 2025. While Beckett was born in North Carolina and the Hammers had settled there, moving back to Venice was always being discussed. item.title: 2027: Ajimobi, Folarin, Adelabu lead Oyo APC reconciliation push
item.description: By Adeola Badru Efforts to resolve internal divisions and strengthen the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Oyo State ahead of the 2027 general elections have gained momentum following a meeting involving prominent party leaders. The meeting, led by former Oyo State First Lady and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Austria, Mrs Florence Ajimobi, brought together the Oyo State Coordinator of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Teslim Kolawole Folarin; Senator Abdulfatai Buhari, representing Oyo North Senatorial District; former Minister of Power, Chief Adebayo Adelabu; and Barrister Akeem Agbaje. The meeting focused on resolving internal disagreements, promoting inclusive leadership and rebuilding unity within the party ahead of the 2027 elections. According to sources familiar with the discussions, participants emphasised the need to set aside personal differences and competing interests in the collective interest of the party. They reportedly agreed that greater cohesion among party leaders and stakeholders would strengthen the APC’s political structure and improve its chances in the state. The discussions also highlighted the importance of sustained consultations among critical stakeholders and ensuring that different tendencies within the party were accommodated in its decision-making process. A major issue raised at the meeting was the need to translate calls for reconciliation into concrete actions aimed at rebuilding trust, addressing grievances and encouraging cooperation among party leaders and members. With the 2027 elections approaching, the engagement was seen as part of renewed efforts by influential party figures to harmonise interests and prevent lingering disagreements from affecting the APC’s preparations. The participants also underscored the importance of developing a collective political strategy capable of carrying all stakeholders along and strengthening the party’s electoral prospects across Oyo State. item.title: Browns CB Denzel Ward weighs in on sudden turn of events for Shedeur Sanders
item.description: [Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union] Browns CB Denzel Ward weighs in on sudden turn of events for Shedeur Sanders appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Cleveland Browns have been one of the most pleasant surprises of the 2026 NFL season. Cleveland is 5-3 headed into Week 9, but they may not have QB Deshaun Watson now that he’s in concussion protocol. That could set the stage for Shedeur Sanders to take over starting duties once again. One Browns defender does not sound worried about that possibility. Browns cornerback Denzel Ward explained his next man up mentality about the quarterback position in a recent interview. “Yeah, that’s the NFL. That’s just, first thought that comes to my mind is next man up mentality always, no matter the position. So quarterback position, DB, so next man up and just got to step up once you get out there,” Ward said on Wednesday, per Camryn Justice. “Whoever’s out there, if Deshaun gets back, great. If Shedeur’s out there, great. And whoever’s out there, we’ll go out there and try to win.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit in the first quarter against the Steelers in Week 8. He was evaluated by the league’s Unaffiliated Neurotrauma Consultant after the play and was cleared to return. Watson also did not show signs of a concussion on Monday after the game. However, Watson’s told Cleveland’s medical team on Tuesday morning that he experienced concussion symptoms on Monday night. Shedeur is expected to start in Week 9 and will take first-team reps at practice this week. It is technically possible to get through concussion protocol in one week and still play. That said, it is much more difficult for quarterbacks than any other position when they do not get first-team reps in practice. Sanders played surprisingly well as a rookie. He logged 1,400 passing yards with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in eight games last year. Now the supporting cast in Cleveland is much improved, so he could play at an even higher level. It will be fascinating to see if Shedeur can lead the Browns to a victory this weekend. Browns at Saints kicks off at 1 p.m. ET on Nov 8 from Caesars Superdome in New Orleans. Related: Browns’ Todd Monken reveals why he’s pumped for Shedeur Sanders to get first start of 2026 Related: What Browns’ Shedeur Sanders said about possibly starting for Deshaun Watson vs. Saints

item.title: Andy Weir's New Sci-Fi Epic is ‘The Martian’ Meets ‘The Twilight Zone’
item.description: Andy Weir is known for his dramatic sci-fi survival stories The Martian and Project Hail Mary , which were both adapted into blockbuster films. His latest project combines the same focus on action and ingenuity, but with a more surreal concept that feels straight out of The Twilight Zone . Weir is executive producing Exoplanet , a full-cast audio experience written by Benjamin Percy for Audible. It follows the crew of the starship Wild Blue Yonder as they are scattered across time, landing on the same planet in different eras. The thriller releases on Nov. 5, and Audible provided Polygon with an exclusive clip following Science Officer Logan Bowers (John Leguizamo of The Odyssey ) as he wakes up injured and desperately tries to find help.

item.title: The hidden supply chain costs of the AI boom
item.description: Today, I’m talking with Willy Shih, an economist, a professor of management practice at Harvard Business School, and the author of the upcoming book, Where Does My Stuff Come From? The Powerful Economics Behind Global Supply Chains . Willy is one of my all-time favorite Decoder guests — his way of looking at the world through our supply chains is just a fascinating way of making sense of the global economy. I first met Willy in 2019, while The Verge was covering Foxconn’s promise to build an LCD fab in Wisconsin. That obviously never happened, but Willy called it right away because he could see the supply chain to support a fab simply wasn’t in place. We also had Willy on the show in 2021 to talk about what was then the pandemic-era chip shortage. Now, five years later, we’re in another manufacturing mess, as we stand in the middle of a political fight over whether globalization is coming to an end. Trumps’ tariffs keep changing, the factories that were supposed to reshore in America mostly haven’t materialized, and AI is devouring the planet’s computing resources during an unprecedented infrastructure buildout. Willy’s new book is all about the economics underlying these complex systems, which our politicians and regulators seem to insistently ignore. You’ll hear us talk about why the markets have reacted to all these disruptions the way they have, and why China remains a global manufacturing powerhouse even though every other country thinks that’s so risky. I loved this conversation — it’s in the weeds, and Willy really knows his stuff. Okay: economist Will Shih on his new book Where Does My Stuff Come From? Here we go. This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity. Willy Shih, you’re an economist and professor of management practice at Harvard. You’re also the author of the new book, Where Does My Stuff Come From: The Powerful Economics Behind Global Supply Chains . Welcome back to Decoder . Well, thanks for having me back. I am very excited to talk to you. You and I first started talking ages ago when The Verge was covering Foxconn in Wisconsin. You are a reliable source of information on what it takes to actually build an LCD plant anywhere, not just in Wisconsin. The Foxconn in Wisconsin thing was funny because I tend to go on first principles on these things. Once I knew they weren’t going to build a glass plant across the street, it’s like there’s no way there’s going to be a factory. Now, what happened afterwards, of course, is people heard your show, and then I started getting calls from people who live in the community. They went to the zoning hearings in town, then sent me the plans and asked, “Is this going to be a panel factory?” I said, “No, I told you it’s not going to be a panel factory.” So they sent me the plans. I said, “Well, there’s not enough concrete to make this a panel factory.” For a panel factory, you need stability, so you gotta have all this structural steel, and you have to have all this concrete. item.title: Earth photobombs spacewalking Canadian astronaut | Space photo of the day for Nov. 5, 2026
item.description: null Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk poses for a photo during his spacewalk on Oct. 29, 2026. (Image credit: CSA) Spacewalks are hard work, so sometimes you need to take a break for a moment and snap a gorgeous selfie with your home planet in the background. What is it? During a pre-Halloween spacewalk on Oct. 29, 2026, Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk took a moment to pose for a photograph. In this moment , the International Space Station to which he was tethered was orbiting 267 miles (430 kilometers) above the South Atlantic Ocean down below on Earth. During this spacewalk — the first for a Canadian since 2019 — Kutryk and NASA astronaut Anil Menon worked together to install a new roll-out solar array on the station while also performing some "get ahead" tasks to prep for the next spacewalk, which is happening today (Nov. 5). During today's excursion, the same two astronauts will venture out into space, tethered to the space station, to install the eighth and final roll-out solar array. These eight new arrays will boost the station's available power by a total of 30%, according to NASA officials. Why is it incredible? When we think of astronauts working in space, we might think of the important science and research they're doing aboard the station. Astronauts work on everything from biomedical research to plant science and physics experiments. But the job also includes work on the space station itself. Sometimes they have to venture out into the vacuum of space to fix urgent problems. These situations can be tense, and there's a lot of pressure to get things absolutely right. But even spacewalks that do relatively mundane maintenance work, like the one on Oct. 29, come with pressure. Every minute that astronauts spend outside of the space station, there are countless risk factors floating around. Earth orbit is a very harsh environment, after all, even if it does allow for some pretty amazing selfies.

item.title: Scouting Report: Merrimack Warriors
item.description: Merrimack’s Matthias Latham tries to leap over Delaware tackler Kevin Moore In the Blue Hens’ 42-7 season opening win at Delaware Stadium, Sept. 3, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Basics Team : Merrimack Warriors Location : North Andover, Massachusetts Enrollment : 4,102 Head Coach : Mike Gennetti (13-19) Record : 4-5 Wins : Maine, New Hampshire, New Haven, Wagner Losses : Rhode Island, Delaware, Tarleton State, Yale, Dartmouth Recruiting Rank : N/A Transfer Portal Rank : N/A Win Total : N/A Spread : Wake -47.5 The annual FCS buy game could not have come at a better time for the Deacs this season—with Gio Lopez’s injury status up in the air, Wake should be able to give him an extra week to potentially heal up before they head to Dallas for a very important game against SMU. Frankly, the Deacs are probably not going to need him to beat a Merrimack team that is 4-4 in FCS games this season and got blown by FBS Delaware 42-7 earlier in the season. Offense Points per game : 18.0 (110 out of 124 FCS teams) Yards per game : 339.6 (74) Run/pass : 56% run, 44% pass Rush yards per game : 162.2 (47) Pass yards per game : 177.3 (93) 3rd down conversions : 32% (106) Sacks allowed per game : 1.33 (25) Turnovers : 19 (114) This probably isn’t going to be a super in depth scouting report because Merrimack has one of the worst offenses in the nation at the FCS level, and the Deacs have one of the best defenses in the nation at the FBS level. The Warriors haven’t scored more than 25 points in a single game this year, and Wake Forest has given up 31 total points in the last month—this is clearly a colossal mismatch in Wake’s favor, and the size, speed, and talent disparity between the two teams is going to be nearly insurmountable for Merrimack. Merrimack is a run first team that has gone for over 150 yards on the ground in 5 of their 9 games this season. The main rusher for the Warriors is running back Matthias Latham, who has carried the ball 122 times for 626 yards (5.1 ypc) and 3 touchdowns this season. The other threat in the backfield is 6-3, 215 pound UMass transfer QB AJ Hairston, who has run for 295 yards and 5 touchdown. In Merrimack’s 1 FBS game this season—against a Delaware team that is allowing 4.2 yards per carry (80th)—the aforementioned duo combined for 11 total rushing yards and the Warriors finished the game with 48 total rushing yards on 25 rushing attempts. The Deacs currently have the 6th best run defense in the nation and have held their last 4 ACC opponents to under 40 yards per game, so stopping Merrimack from moving the ball on the ground should not be an issue at all. In the passing game, Merrimack hasn’t been great. Last season, as a member of the 0-12 UMass Minutemen, Hairston completed 50% of his passes for 957 yards, 4 touchdowns, and 4 interceptions. item.title: Henley Anderson shines bright for Texas volleyball despite the 'ring of fire'
item.description: Texas Longhorns outside hitter Henley Anderson (22) takes the court ahead of the game against Alabama in Gregory Gym on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Despite being a freshman for Texas volleyball this season, Henley Anderson has had to maneuver a "ring of fire," according to her coach. After outside hitter Abby Vander Wal suffered an ACL injury at the end of August, Anderson has had to fill her role since the third game of the season. Jerritt Elliott recognizes just how difficult that can be for a first-year player. "When you're freshmen, the pressure and everything else you go through, it's really hard to kind of perform at a high level and it's overwhelming," Elliott said in August. Henley showed power and potential early, but she had to deal with a steep learning curve as Texas played seven top-25 teams before conference play. Plus she had to get used to being a main scoring option for the Longhorns with outside hitters Torrey Stafford and Cari Spears . Elliott kept telling her to "go be Henley Anderson" and as SEC play has gone on, the Dripping Springs product has settled in nicely. UP NEXT NO. 13 TEXAS VS. MISSOURI When/where: 7 p.m. Friday in Columbia, Mo. TV: SEC Network+. In Sunday's win over A&M , Anderson had 10 kills and hit .444 in the Longhorns' sweep, which earned her a third SEC freshman of the week accolade. Elliott said he has seen her grow in a short time. "Early in the year she was just a one-trick pony," Elliott said Sunday. "Now she's doing a lot of different things: adding tips and high-line shots, learning how to tool the block, hitting deep corner, hitting hard cross. She's starting to learn how to be a real volleyball player." MORE: ‘Like playing with MJ': Nya Bunton bided time behind greats. Will it help 2026 Longhorns? MORE: Ramsey Gary flashed special determination as a toddler. Now it's helping Texas Longhorns How does Anderson stack up against other SEC freshmen? Anderson had a career-high 15 kills in the five-set match against SMU . She had seven kills against Wisconsin and combined for 12 in the first pair of SEC games. As the conference slate has continued, she's up to 11.2 kills per match through the last nine games and is becoming a dangerous part of No. 13 Texas' rotation. The Texas Longhorns celebrate beating Texas A&M in the Lone Star Showdown volleyball match at Gregory Gym on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) And she's making a strong case for SEC freshman of the year honors, too. Henley has won the conference's weekly freshman award in three of the last five weeks. Georgia's Gigi Artiles is the only other outside hitters to be named the freshman of the week at least once. Artiles is second on the Bulldogs in kills and was the first named freshman of the week this season after 10 kills and hitting .444 against North Florida and 12 kills and hitting .579 against Furman. item.title: Broncos vs. Panthers: 3 Things to Watch in Week 9
item.description: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: J.K. Dobbins #27 of the Denver Broncos after defeating the Arizona Cardinals 30-16 at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos have a chance to notch their seventh victory of the season on Sunday. The Carolina Panthers stand in the way of the Broncos becoming winners of five in a row. Here are three storylines I’ll be watching closely in Denver’s Week 9 matchup. Who gets the lead role in the Broncos’ backfield? Earlier this morning, I gave my thoughts on how the Broncos can beat the Panthers. My first major point was getting the run game going. The Panthers have a bottom 5 run defense in the National Football League and it’s clearly their biggest weakness as a team. I think the Broncos will try and take advantage of this. However, I’ll be interested to see how the carries shake out for the Broncos. Without RJ Harvey, the Broncos three-headed rushing attack is down to just J.K. Dobbins and rookie Jonah Coleman. In the second half of the Chiefs game, Dobbins was virtually absent from the field. Coleman dominated the second half playing time and went on to notch 104 all-purpose yards, a touchdown, and had several big plays that helped guide the Broncos to a huge victory. Yesterday, Head Coach Sean Payton was asked whether or not the Broncos are trying to manage Dobbins’ workload. Payton seemed to imply that the media and fans are making a bigger deal of his second half absence versus the Chiefs than anyone inside Dove Valley is. “He’s a huge part of what we’re doing. Each week we look at—a lot of times who’s the back that’s in there with the hot hand. But he’s been fantastic. To answer your question: No, that’s not a hot button topic with us here. It might be with you guys, but not with us. We’re good. We’re good with the rotation,” stated Payton. Dobbins has carried the ball 94 times this season for 306 yards and 3 touchdowns. His 3.3 yard per carry average is the second worst of any running back in the NFL who has at least 90 carries on the season. While Coleman’s body of work is limited, it’s quite obvious he is the ‘hot hand’ in Denver’s group of running backs and should be in store for more carries. Payton has always said it’s easier to gameplan for two running backs as opposed to three. With that in mind, I’m quite curious to see who ends up getting a majority of the work in the ground game versus the Panthers. Will it be an even split or will one back prevail as the clear-cut favorite? Will rookie Tyler Onyedim see his first action of the season? The Broncos were able to come away with a big victory last week against the Chiefs. Unfortunately, several players exited the game with injury and may not be able to go versus the Panthers on Sunday. Those would be cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, safety Brandon Jones, and defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike. None of them participated in yesterday’s practice session . If Uwazurike i

item.title: Time for Texans to put their money where their mouth is…
item.description: We’ve been hearing it over and over for the last 2 years: the Texans want to play hat-on-hat, smash-mouth football. An aggressive, “establish the run” sort of offense that the Erhardt-Perkins offensive scheme flourishes with, when done properly. Unfortunately, offensive coordinator Nick Caley and offensive line coach/run game coordinator Cole Popovich have been unable to pull this rabbit out of their (un)imaginary hat. Last year, it was easy to point the finger at the mysterious injury/illness/medical foot condition of running back Joe Mixon. To rectify this in the off-season, general manager Nick Caserio traded for former Detroit Lion RB2 David Montgomery, who was promptly injured. Now, it all seems to fall on Woody Marks and a jumbo-package of basic run plays that wouldn’t fool the local High School defense, much less an NFL one. Marks is a great runner, but not a one-man Houston Texans running back depth chart. Despite mountains of evidence to make a case that the coaching is largely to blame, both in what the coaches are teaching the players and what plays Caley is calling, head coach Demeco Ryans seems to think the players are at fault, 100%. Well, if it’s a player problem, then here’s a player solution: Update: Teams have reached out to the Ravens regarding a potential trade for RB Derrick Henry, per league source. pic.twitter.com/4B1AViI8Lo — NFL Talk (@NFL_Talk_Sports) November 4, 2026 While Derrick Henry might be 33 and nearing the end of the road, he still has plenty of gas in the tank. And, on a team with Woody Marks and C.J. Stroud, he wouldn’t have to carry the entire load like he’s currently expected to do with the Baltimore Ravens. An aging lion is still lethal and threatening. Even if only the threat of him is enough to make opposing defenses fear the run some of the time. Derrick Henry on if he feels he needs to carry the team with all the injuries at QB: pic.twitter.com/H0s6QMvuHN — Jamison Hensley (@jamisonhensley) November 2, 2026 So far in 2026, Henry has carried the ball 158 times for 632 yards at a 4.0 yard per carry average. He’s also caught 12 of 14 passes for 75 yards. All this has added 9 touchdowns to the Ravens 2026 totals. Enough to put him in 7th place in the current running back Top 10. Meaning, an aging Henry is still better than most of the running backs in the NFL. 9 more touchdowns on the Texans season moves them to 5-2, if not 6-1. While other teams, such as the New York Giants, might go hard in the paint to get Henry, the Texans are at make-or-break time for the current regime. We’ve already gone over , ad nauseum, how bad Caserio, Ryans, Caley, defensive coordinator Matt Burke and Popovich have squandered the off-season hype and fan goodwill. Continuing down the current path of failure leads to the McNair’s having no choice but to fire some or all of them. Often in these situations, embattled GMs and coaches will make Hail Mary trades to attempt to salvage a make or break, one player away season. With Caseri

item.title: 3 bold predictions for Michigan Football vs Michigan State
item.description: ANN ARBOR, MI - OCTOBER 26: Michigan Wolverines defensive end Josaiah Stewart (0) and the team celebrate their 24-17 victory to keep the Paul Bunyan Trophy during the Michigan Wolverines versus the Michigan State Spartans game on Saturday October 26, 2024 at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor, MI. (Photo by Steven King/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images This weekend, the Michigan Wolverines are trying to do something they haven’t done since Sept. 19: win back-to-back games. The Wolverines beat Western Michigan, Oklahoma and UTEP to open the season, but have gone loss, loss, win, loss, win since then. That trend needs to end this weekend against Michigan State. While last week offered some encouragement in a few areas, it was a performance that left most fans disappointed. Rutgers is as bad as it gets in the Big Ten, and despite out-gaining the Scarlet Knights by nearly 200 yards, only allowing three completions, gaining 14 more first downs and nearly doubling up in time of possession, it was a one-score game that came down to the wire. Like we’ve seen so many times this season, the Wolverines played down to their competition. They were fortunate to win, but in a rivalry game, that won’t fly. Let’s make some bold predictions for this weekend’s matchup against Michigan State. Michigan will double Michigan State’s yardage There’s no doubt about it, Michigan is more talented than Michigan State. Does that mean the Wolverines are going to win? No. Michigan is also more talented than Iowa and Minnesota, and we saw how those games went. Still, the talent advantage will play a factor. Both teams struggle offensively, as the Wolverines (second-worst in the Big Ten) and Spartans (worst) have the two worst offenses in the Big Ten. However, Michigan has a massive advantage defensively. In total defense in all of college football, Michigan is ranked No. 3 out of 138 while Michigan State is No. 64. The Wolverines have a championship level defense and are going up against an offense that is depleted and struggling. Based on that alone, the Wolverines shouldn’t have an issue winning the game if they play clean football and don’t beat themselves. I think Michigan will at least double up MSU in the yardage department. Michigan will miss 3+ field goals Speaking of beating themselves, one big issue that has added itself to the mix the last couple weeks has been the kicking game. If a 32-yard field goal is made against Indiana, Michigan probably wins that game, and without more missed kicks against Rutgers, that game is a lot less stressful down the stretch. Trey Butkowski has missed four field goals the last two weeks, and two of them were from 35 yards or closer. The Wolverines have opened up the kicking competition this week, but even if it’s someone new, it’s a college kicker taking his first career kicks under the lights in front of 110,000+ people in a rivalry game. item.title: Mets International Free Agent Profile: Jyun-Yue Tseng
item.description: TOKYO, JAPAN - MARCH 07: Jyun-Yue Tseng #60 of Team Chinese Taipei throws in the seventh inning during the 2026 World Baseball Classic Pool C game between Chinese Taipei and Czechia at Tokyo Dome on March 7, 2026 in Tokyo, Japan. (Photo by Toru Hanai/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jyun-Yue Tseng was born on November 7, 2001 in Taichung, Taiwan’s second-largest city behind Taipei. He attended the verbosely named Taichung Municipal Taichung Industrial High School and developed into a standout baseball player, at first as an infielder and later as a pitcher. On July 20, 2020, he was one of 123 amateur players to enter into the CPBL Draft, and the right-hander was one of 48 players who were selected by a professional club, with the Fubon Guardians picking him in the seventh round of the process. The 19-year-old Tseng made his professional debut in 2021 and quickly established himself as one of the preeminent relievers in the league, appearing in 57 games and posting a 1.80 ERA in 55.0 innings, allowing 36 hits, walking 16, and striking out 62 while saving 12 games. For his efforts, he was named the 2021 Rookie of the Year. He followed up his Rookie of the Year campaign with statistically similar seasons over the next few years, cementing himself as one of Taiwan’s best relief pitchers. In 2022, he posted a 2.86 ERA in 50.1 innings over 47 games, allowing 35 hits, walking 18, and striking out 64 while saving 20 games. In 2023, he posted a 1.22 ERA in 51.2 innings over 54 appearances, allowing 29 hits, walking 17, and striking out 60 while saving 18 games. After the 2023 season ended, Tseng was able to get the Guardians to post him, but he did not find much of a market outside of Taiwan and opted to remained with Fubon. In 2024, he posted a 1.52 ERA in 47.1 innings, allowing 36 hits, walking 14, and striking out 63 while saving 6 games. His streak of utter dominance ended in 2025, when he posted a 3.00 ERA in 36.0 innings over 34 games, allowing 30 hits, walking 13, and striking out 28. Yue returned to the Taiwanese National Team in the 2026 World Baseball Classic, appearing in a pair of games and notching a single save, throwing 2.0 scoreless innings, not allowing a hit or a walk while striking out two. Returning to the Guardians for the regular season, the right-hander would go on to post a 1.57 ERA in 51.2 innings, allowing 48 hits, walking 13, and striking out 65 while saving 25 games. After the season ended, the 24-year-old right-hander filed for international free agency and the posting request was approved by the Guardians. The 5’8”, 150-pound right-hander would be one of the shortest pitchers in Major League Baseball. He throws from a high-three-quarters arm slot with a long arm action through the back, utilizing a hitch in his leg lift and wrapping his wrist during the full extension of his arm circle. item.title: Chargers open activation windows for TE Njoku, LB Perryman
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 13: David Njoku #83 of the Los Angeles Chargers walks off the field following an NFL game between the Arizona Cardinals and the Los Angeles Chargers on September 13, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Greg Fiore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Wednesday, Jim Harbaugh told reporters ahead of practice that the team would be opening the 21-day activation windows for both tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman. Activating both of these players would leave the Chargers with three remaining activations from IR for the remainder of the 2026 season. Njoke joined the Chargers as a free agent this offseason and began his tenure with the Bolts on a high note through the team’s first two games, catching five passes for 58 yards against the Raiders before leaving that game with an injury. Perryman has been on IR since before the regular season began. In his place, former undrafted free agent Del’Shawn Phillips has been the starter in the middle alongside Daiyan Henley. His return would bring back a veteran presence with plenty of experience, which is a positive even if the defense has been getting by just fine through injuries to that side of the ball. With the Chargers going down to three remaining activations this year, they will have to make some tough choices about who is worth bringing back and who isn’t. Right now, left tackle Rashawn Slater, safety Derwin James, offensive lineman Trey Pipkins, fullback Alec Ingold, and backup quarterback Trey Lance are all on IR. Slater and James are certainly going to take two of those spots — if it’s even worth bringing them back in a season such as this — but who ends up being that last activation? Perhaps it is someone who hasn’t been injured yet. Holding it for later could actually be the smart choice.

item.title: Breaking down the 2026 Section 2 Class A football playoffs
item.description: Quarterback Kyair Carr hopes to lead Troy to a Class A title. (Jim Franco/Times Union) The Section 2 Class A football playoffs start Friday with semifinal play. Out of the four programs remaining, two of them experienced losing seasons in 2025. The Super Bowl is set to take place Nov. 13 at Colonie High School. Here is a breakdown of the 2026 Class A playoffs. Semifinal matchups No. 4 Mohonasen (5-4) at No. 1 Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake (9-0), Friday, 7 p.m. No. 3 Queensbury (5-4) at No. 2 Troy (7-2), Friday, 7 p.m. Things to know Mohonasen enters the playoffs with its first five-win season since 2005. The program has dropped nine straight playoff games, starting with a 41-20 Class A semifinal loss to Averill Park in 2005. The last eight losses came in quarterfinal contests in eight-team sectional fields. Overall, Mohonasen is 3-13 in its sectional history, which began in 1996, including consecutive losses against Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake in 2011 (47-6), 2012 (68-6) and 2013 (67-8). … Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake finished 4-6 in 2025, bowing out in the quarterfinals. The Spartans (9-0) last won nine games in 2021 and seek their first 10-win season since 2017. … Troy is 3-0 against Queensbury in sectional semifinal contests. Overall, the Flying Horses own a 9-4 record against the Spartans in all meetings. … Queensbury is making its third straight semifinal appearance. Troy defeated the Spartans 39-16 in the 2025 semifinals. Player to watch There are a number of weapons that opponents must contend with when facing the Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake offense. In particular, junior Talon Immel has provided many memorable moments for the Spartans this season at running back. Immel, a recent University at Albany men's lacrosse commit who missed two games earlier this season while competing for the 17-and-under USA national lacrosse team, delivered a season-best 165 yards and two touchdowns in a 28-6 win against Guilderland. How did James Allen do? I selected three correct teams in my preseason choices : Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake, Queensbury and Troy. The team I missed on, well, represents the worst win/loss gaffe I have experienced in 30 years of making preseason football predictions. Not only did Mohonasen qualify for the postseason for the second time in 10 years, it did so with a 5-4 overall record and garnered the No. 4 seed. My prediction was - gulp - for Mohonasen to finish ninth out of nine teams at 0-9. Needless to say, this was a colossal whiff on my part. Considering Mohonasen combined to go 6-23 from 2023-25, this season's squad has surpassed the expectations of even its most ardent supporters. Prediction time The best team all season in the classification has been Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake, a squad that prevailed during the regular season against each of the other playoff squads with wins against Troy (28-14), Queensbury (42-7) and Mohonasen (42-7). item.title: Saints Rookie Report: Week 9 preview vs. the Browns
item.description: METAIRIE, LOUISIANA - AUGUST 13: Jordyn Tyson #0 of the New Orleans Saints participates in drills during a joint practice at Ochsner Sports Performance Center on August 13, 2026 in Metairie, Louisiana. (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming out of the bye week, the New Orleans Saints made some needed changes, and now they have to show that a real impact was made. The rookies can make that happen. WR Jordyn Tyson Finally, it’s time for Tyson’s debut. Right away, Tyson’s addition to the team will massively help the offense. It takes pressure away from Chris Olave, allows Tyler Shough to have yet another incredible weapon, adds the threat of a dynamic player after the catch, and could open up the run game. The issue is it won’t solve the run game issues. The Saints will have a lot of work to do on the offensive side of the ball, and although Tyson’s addition helps, it will be for nothing if the rushing attack and offensive line continue with their struggles. DT Christen Miller Out of the bye week, there is absolutely no reason for Christen Miller to be benched. He is the future at the Saints’ defensive tackle spot; he should be the best run defender as well. He will develop with reps. Even if the Saints end up not starting him, he should be playing way more snaps than he has so far. It’s time to see what the Saints have in their second-round pick. TE Oscar Delp Similar to Miller, Delp must be elevated to a larger role in the offense. He has primarily been utilized as a blocker, which has created a tell in the offense. Trying to play on that and trick the Browns could be reallt smart, and a way to do that is by using Delp as a receiver more. Noah Fant hasn’t been bad this season, but Delp should be TE2 moving forward. OG Jeremiah Wright News on Cesar Ruiz’s injury has not been released yet, so it’s unknown if Wright is going play, but if he does, good luck to him. The Browns defensive line is very good and it’s going to be his biggest test yet. He wasn’t horrible against the Steelers, but it was also not good and he looked like a rookie out there. That’s the expectation, but the Saints will need to see more from him against the Browns. WR Bryce Lance With Tyson’s return, it’s going to be interesting to see how the Saints use Lance. He will now be WR4/5 with Barion Brown, and although his involvement in the passing game will likely drop, his blocking is too important to not use. Also, special teams may be an option for him. WR Barion Brown Recently, Brown has been more involved in the offense, and it has had a positive impact. Like with Lance, Brown’s role will likely be reduced in the passing game, but I wouldn’t be shocked to see him utilized as a deep play threat throughout games. Then on special teams, he has been better recently, which is definitely nice to see for New Orleans. RB CJ Donaldson CJ Donaldson is in a weird situation. He has had some good runs and great blocks, but not consistently, and although Kendre Miller may

item.title: Commanders safety Nick Cross has greater alignment diversity than any NFL defender - Daily Slop
item.description: SANTA CLARA, CA - OCTOBER 19: Nick Cross #25 of the Washington Commanders exits the field during an NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 5 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links a night to remember pic.twitter.com/WjJnkEooj7 — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 4, 2026 Articles Sports Illustrated Commanders’ Unique Usage of Safety Nick Cross Could Have Long-Term Implications Nick Cross’ expanded slot role gives Washington more options and could influence Mike Sainristil’s playing time and how the secondary is built Washington Commanders safety Nick Cross has greater alignment diversity than any NFL defender, according to SumerSports data through Week 8. The interesting part is that Cross’ position designation captures only part of what defensive coordinator Daronte Jones asks him to do. So, then the real question becomes: What does Washington gain by moving him around this much? Cross gives Jones a 212-pound safety who can play closer to the run game and be used as a blitzer. He can also move back to a deeper alignment on the next snap. Washington doesn’t have to take him off the field to change his job. Cross earned his two highest overall PFF grades of the season against San Francisco and Philadelphia. The Eagles game was also his strongest in run defense and tackling, backing up what Quinn saw near the line. Moving Cross around only helps if the other ten defenders are on the same page. Cross’ work at nickel also gives Jones an alternative to Mike Sainristil , who didn’t play a defensive snap against Philadelphia. Cross still has something to prove in coverage. PFF has charged him with 10 receptions on 11 targets for 69 yards and one touchdown across four appearances, with a 56.2 coverage grade. Those catches averaged 6.9 yards, so opponents haven’t piled up yardage in that sample. The figures include all his coverage work, not just his plays from the slot. If Cross proves he can cover consistently from the slot, Washington could have less need for a dedicated nickel corner. That would give general manager Adam Peters more flexibility to prioritize outside corners or depth elsewhere in the secondary. item.title: Panthers vs Broncos: Key Storylines to watch
item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Tetairoa McMillan #4 of the Carolina Panthers warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Panthers get to return from their mini bye following two crushing losses to the Buccaneers and the Packers. They fired their defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero following these games, if you hadn’t heard. Funny enough, they’ll be taking on the Broncos, the team Evero coached for as a DC prior to Carolina poaching him up. This Broncos team is a different iteration compared to that one, as they were a QB injury away from going to the Super Bowl last season and currently sit at 6-2 atop their division for a playoff berth. The Panthers also sit atop their division, albeit with very different circumstances and definitely a seemingly different direction. The Panthers will need to stop the losing skid they are on soon if they want to reclaim control of their season, where the Broncos have the Chiefs nipping right at their heels for control of the division. Let’s dive right into all the key storylines.‘ Defense: Contain Bo Nix The easy story to talk about is the Panthers rushing defense, ranked in the bottom of the league in most categories. However, Denver’s rushing attacks ranks in the mid 20s in the league in yards per rush, yards per game, and rushes per game via TeamRankings.com. The Panthers will also be making a concerted effort to stop the run per Dave Canales this week following their changing of the guard in the coaching staff, so instead I’d like to highlight another problem that has plagued them in losses this year; mobile quarterbacks. EDGE Patrick Jones talked about being more aggressive, specifically along the defensive front, and getting into the backfield more. Nix hasn’t been AS damaging as a rusher this season, averaging short of 4 yards per attempt. But believe me, the man can get away from some pressure and keep plays alive. I would expect the Panthers to unveil an attacking forward defensive approach this week, and rattling Bo Nix will be the best way to keep them in this game. Offense: Dear god offensive line PLEASE The story of the last several weeks has been the Panthers allowing pressure on basically half of their passing snaps. For an offense that cut its teeth early on in the season with aggressive passing down the field, that’s a really bad thing. It was especially apparent against the Packers, as they not only sacked Bryce Young 6 times, but they batted down a ton of passing attempts even when they didn’t get home on the rush. This offensive line is allowing a free rusher at the quarterback at an alarming rate, and they need to figure that out one way or the other. Maybe they execute more rollouts and waggle plays where they get Bryce Young moving, maybe they bring in extra blockers at tight end in the backfield or to chip as they run out on their passes. Either

item.title: The Seahawks are living in the worst of both worlds in the red zone
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks are 4-4, just lost by 17 points to the Chicago Bears on Monday night, yet still have a +26 point differential. Turnovers have obviously been a huge factor in three of their four defeats, but a season-long issue for Seattle’s offense and defense has been seemingly unshakeable. Neither unit is getting the job done in the red zone. Seattle’s offense is one of the worst in the red zone Seattle’s offense ranks a dismal 29th in red zone touchdown percentage, scoring just 13 TDs on 28 trips. If you look at points per red zone trip, which obviously includes field goals, Seattle still ranks 29th. For whatever reason, even though red zone performance is supposedly a high-variance statistic, the Seahawks have not once fielded a top-16 offense in points per red zone possession in the post-Russell Wilson era. This is currently the worst Seahawks offense in the red zone since 2016, when they had a mostly injured Wilson at quarterback, a heavily injured running back unit, and an offensive line that was a total horror show. While the red zone encompasses the 20-yard line and in, there’s an observation I’ve made throughout the season with Brian Fleury’s playcalling. When the Seahawks are faced with a goal-to-go situation, Fleury’s default move is to run the ball to mixed (at best) results. I’m not joking: 12 runs to 1 pass. The pass was a touchdown to Cooper Kupp in the hurry-up offense against the Washington Commanders, by the way. I present to you every Seahawks goal-to-go play on 1st down this season, with the exception of a kneeldown against the Chargers. The Seahawks are the only team in the NFL with a 1st down run rate above 90% in goal-to-go situations. pic.twitter.com/ciZqYtv2TH — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) November 5, 2026 No other team (at least using Stathead play-by-play data ) is this run-heavy on first-and-goal than Seattle. Only the New York Giants and Cleveland Browns have thrown it once on first-and-goal. Last season, the Seahawks had a pass-run ratio of 14:19 on first-and-goal, and while the red zone offense was also lackluster under Klint Kubiak, they were not extraordinarily predictable. The first-and-goal runs are not the main reason Seattle is a poor red zone offense, but it’s certainly a factor. We’ve seen very little play-action in the red zone on any down, and the Seahawks roster generally lacks a true “go up and get it” receiving target. That last bit is mostly opinion, but you can probably count the number of high-point catches made by Seahawks receivers on one hand this year—Jaxon Smith-Njigba included. It’s not a strength of this roster and it has to be something Seattle considers when it inevitably examines how to improve the offense next season. Seattle’s red zone defense is the worst in the NFL This part is stunning. The Seahawks defense as a whole is still playing very well, but they’re losing in the key situational areas at an alarming rate. They rank 32nd in red zone efficiency, conceding touchdowns

item.title: 3 Keys to Victory for Ravens-Jaguars Week 9
item.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Joe Fagnano #12 of the Baltimore Ravens throws a pass against the Buffalo Bills during an NFL football game at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Ravens have a Thursday night game coming off another bad loss in Buffalo. They are once again without Lamar Jackson with the rest of their season shrouded in uncertainty. For now, Baltimore is trying to stay afloat after laying the groundwork to acquire Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals. But first, preseason standout Joe Fagnano will start his first NFL game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Can the Ravens somehow stay above .500 with the undrafted rookie at the helm? If they have any chance, they’ll have to follow these three keys: Get the ball out quick An offensive line is clearly in bad shape when they let three quarterbacks get injured while dropping back to pass in the same game. Even after Jackson and Tyler Huntley went down in Buffalo, the Ravens struggled to make protection adjustments and did not prioritize getting the ball out quickly. Right guard Vega Ioane is returning to from a one-game absence, so for just the second time in nine games, the Ravens’ desired starting five offensive linemen will be on the field. The first time was against the Bengals two weeks ago, but that lasted less than a quarter before Ioane’s injury Upgrading the weakest link at right guard should lead to improvements for the unit. That may not be saying much considering the rock-bottom showing in Buffalo, but this group can be at least average, if not gel into something greater than its parts. But until they do, Declan Doyle needs to help Fagnano in his first start. Minimize his processing with quick reads and designed touches that minimize the chance for costly sacks and turnovers. If the line holds, Doyle can consider mixing him some longer-developing route concepts that could give Fagnano a chance to push the ball downfield, like he did in the preseason. Lean on Henry The Ravens’ run game might be helped even more by a health O-line. Ioane’s big, physical presence will be next to zone-specialist center Cam Jurgens for a full game (hopefully) for the first time. Derrick Henry had a solid start to the year behind a more consistent line , scoring seven touchdowns with 374 yards in the first four games. He had another 100-yard performance in the first game without Lamar Jackson in Atlanta, but since then, it’s been three straight games under 60 yards. He looked better in the Buffalo game, scoring his first touchdown since Week 4 and averaging 4.8 yards per carry, but he only got 11 carries. Now the Ravens have a short week, a rookie undrafted quarterback making his first career, a finally-healthy offensive line, and an opponent that Henry has terrorized during his time in Tennessee. item.title: Bears-Seahawks Upon Further Review: A Closer Look at the Referees
item.description: Nov 2, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Chicago Bears defensive line Grady Jarrett (50) questions a call with the officials during the first half against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Monday Night, November 2, 2026. Lumen Field, Seattle. Crew: Shawn Smith (R #14), Tra Blake (U #3), Jay Bilbo (DJ #84), Jeff Seeman (LJ #45), Dyrol Prioleau (FJ #109), Keith Parham (SJ #41), Dino Paganelli (BJ #105), Mike Wimmer (RO #0). Hello Chicago Bears fans! Chicago flew to Seattle on Monday night and departed with a 34–17 statement victory in Big Jeff’s first game. But let’s dive into the calls and no-calls in the game. The Hawks fans are squawking, but we here at UFR take a bird’s-eye view on the calls in the game and no amount of fan noise will ruffle our feathers. Official totals: Bears 10–85 , Seahawks 5–43 . The accepted tape is not, however, where the true story lies. Several judgment calls went against Seattle; several others, however, went against Chicago. One delay of game erased a tackle-for-loss and became the spark for a scoring drive. The same four-tier scale is applied to every accepted flag and every meaningful no-call: Correct, Arguable, Incorrect, Horrible. Weight runs 1–4 by impact (1 for housekeeping, 2 for drive disruption, 3 for scoring or red-zone leverage, 4 for wiped score/turnover or game-ending leverage). Replay overturns are judged against the “clear and obvious” standard. No-calls receive the same grades and weights as thrown flags. The goal is a transparent differential, not a birdbrained screed. The crew under Shawn Smith is under the microscope, but for the most part they were right, so I’m afraid the Hawks fans will be eating crow after this UFR. The Flag of the Game is the fourth-quarter delay of game on Chicago that erased a Seahawks tackle for loss on D’Andre Swift and, on the next snap, set up Kalif Raymond’s 39-yard lateral that put the ball on the five yard line, goal-to-go. The League File is the clear Kyle Williams touchdown that was initially ruled incomplete in the Patriots–Dolphins game. Same method. Same scale. Full breakdown follows. First Quarter CHI 7, SEA 0 (after the opening 17-play, 80-yard drive that ended with Caleb Williams’ 1-yard touchdown to Luther Burden). No-call: Hit on Sam Darnold while sliding. Darnold scrambled on third-and-8 from the Seattle 31. Devin Bush hit him as he went to the ground. No flag. Shawn Smith’s pool-report explanation: “He was scrambling and became a runner. We didn’t see any contact to his head and neck area when he hit the ground.” Darnold had left the pocket and was a runner at the moment of contact. The protection that attaches to a quarterback in the act of passing does not attach once he is a runner. Correct (no-call). Wt 2. How have we gotten so soft in the football community that this is supposed to be a penalty? Darnold is still in the process of his slide and Bush hit him with his back. J

item.title: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 preview and predictions: Can Sami Zayn actually pull this off?
item.description: With no shortage of controversy in the build-up , WWE is moving forward with its annual Crown Jewel event this Saturday in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Featuring two champion vs. champion clashes, a last man standing match and a tag-team title bout, Crown Jewel has the potential to shake things up just weeks before Survivor Series: WarGames — and that isn't even factoring in both Money in the Bank briefcases, which are still waiting to be cashed in. As usual, to get you ready for the PLE, Uncrowned's Horsemen are here to answer several key questions and offer their predictions for the Saturday matinee. Let's ride! WWE appears determined to move forward with its Saudi plans, regardless of tensions within the region. ASSOCIATED PRESS 1. Sum up your thoughts on WWE's decision to keep Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia. Does it impact your excitement or anticipation for the event? Robert Jackman: Where to start? I think this is a much more controversial decision than the call WWE made to run the original Crown Jewel in the wake of Jamal Khashoggi's killing back in 2018. Back then, WWE was defying what looked like a growing international boycott campaign. But as distasteful as it might have been to jet to Riyadh after a state-sanctioned killing of a dissident, Vince McMahon's WWE wasn't putting the whole company in the middle of an active warzone or defying any official travel advisories. As shocking as it is, this is exactly the sort of risk I had in mind when WWE made the big call to ramp up its Saudi partnership at the beginning of last year. Getting three times (at least) the revenue for your stadium shows without having to depend on pesky ticket sales sounds great on the face of it. But when you're taking a massive chunk of your event revenue from a single buyer, one that just happens to be an absolute monarchy in one of the world's least stable regions, it looks very different. Does it dampen my excitement for Saturday's show? I mean, this is the Crown Jewel championship we're talking about here … the champion of champions. The prize position on the WWE podium. How could I not be excited for that, right? Sorry, just practicing my corporate spiel in case I ever get recruited by TKO to the dark side. Drake Riggs: It's stupid and unnecessary, yet entirely unsurprising. I haven't wasted too much energy on this whole debacle because WWE has been treading water for so long. But it's just annoying, and you hope for everyone's safety above all else. I still wish we would see a majority of the roster stick up for themselves and say no to these kinds of things as a collective unit. Theoretically, it should be much easier to do that in an industry like pro-wrestling compared to, let's say, MMA. That being said, the geopolitical situation doesn't change my overall excitement level for this card, which really only has a few things to look forward to anyway. WWE President and TKO Director Nick Khan alongside Saudi financier Turki Alalshikh. Cooper Neill via Getty Images Ke

item.title: Elephant Rumblings: Athletics’ Building Of New Front Office Continues
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - JUNE 23: Major League Baseball Commissioner Rob Manfred (L) and principal owner John Fisher of the Athletics shake hands after participating in a ceremonial groundbreaking for the USD 1.75 billion, 33,000-seat domed stadium for MLB's Athletics on June 23, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The ballpark is being built on nine acres of the 35-acre former site of the Tropicana Las Vegas, which was imploded in October 2024. The A's expect to have the ballpark ready for Opening Day in 2028. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Friday Junior everyone! The Athletics have decided on Brewers executive Cam Castro as their next General Manager. Like most modern front offices in the sport these days, the GM title isn’t what it once was. The top job is now President of Baseball Operations, the job that went to Taylor Smith recently. Even with that being said, the GM job is an important one one way or the other, and it looks like the A’s landed on a good pick for their next one. Castro’s time with the Brewers saw him help draft and develop tons of talented pitchers. Just looking at a list of former pitchers for the Brew Crew over the past decade and you see tons of quality starting pitching such Corbin Burnes, Brandon Woodruff, Freddy Peralta, and more recently Jacob Misiorowski. And then you have studs in the bullpen seemingly every year, with the team able to say bye to Josh Hader and Devin Williams and simply plug in Trevor Megill, who had a dominant season as Milwaukee’s closer (and could be on the trade market). Smith himself comes from more of an analytical background but also oversaw good pitching development at his previous stops in Tampa and Boston. It’s likely Smith is going to be the big-picture voice of the front office moving forward while Castro is in charge of the pitching development. That’s a tall task for this organization, one that has struggled to produce consistent pitching at the big league level. While Castro’s primary focus is likely to be on revamping the farm and the development system, don’t be surprised to see the A’s connected to names he might be familiar with from his days in Milwaukee. If baseball ends up with a salary floor, could we see the A’s make a play for former Brewers ace Freddy Peralta? That’d sure be one way to soak up all that sudden payroll space. Maybe the team is enamored with one of Milwaukee’s young pitchers like Logan Henderson, Robert Gasser or Aaron Ashby, all of whom are young and fit the A’s timeline. Could Castro convince Smith that trading four years of first baseman Nick Kurtz in exchange for four years of an ace in Henderson? If the A’s believe in Tommy White, that’s not the worst trade idea in the world. The A’s are going to be making moves in their pitching department this offseason. Long live the king. For now, at least as No. 1 New Canaan has fallen , the vacuum filled by the conqueror, Fairfield Ludlowe. And now the whole 2026 season has taken a sharp turn into the wilderness. What once seemed like a certainty is now shrouded in the unknown as we navigate this new path toward the playoffs, from which some new opportunities are sure to emerge. Exciting stuff. So expect plenty of playoff spice in this week's Audibles as we start to kick the tires and check the oil on our contenders for the stretch run. It's a week or so too early to make any kind of prediction, so the best we can do is give teams an idea of where they might stand with three full weeks of the season left to play. Right now? The answer is simple: Just win, baby. There's a delicious menu of games from which to choose this week. Now-No. 3 New Canaan will attempt to redeem itself against unbeaten No. 2-ranked St. Joseph, is your main course. Lyman Hall at jilted No. 5 Hand (down from 4) in an SCC unbeaten battle, a showdown just up the shoreline involving Branford and Guilford, plus two big CCC games between Windsor and Maloney and New Britain and Southington on Thursday night. item.title: Syracuse women’s basketball: three takeaways from the Orange’s win over Sacred Heart
item.description: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 06: ead coach Felisha Legette-Jack of the Syracuse Orange smiles during the ACC basketball tip off at Hilton Charlotte Uptown on October 06, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Matt Kelley/Getty Images) | Getty Images A new Syracuse Orange women’s basketball season is underway, and the team opened the year on Tuesday handling business as expected. Syracuse cruised to a 28-point season-opening win at home against Sacred Heart, moving to 1-0 on the young season. Here are three takeaways from victory number one of 2026-27: “Final” rotation is still TBD The early non-con games where Syracuse has the clear talent advantage usually lead to big leads and tons of opportunity across the roster. Coach Felisha Legette-Jack certainly went deep into her bench against Sacred Heart. All 13 players saw minutes on Tuesday, with 11 playing at least 13 minutes. Uche Izoje (team-high 16 points and 14 rebounds) led the team in minutes with just 24. Two initial thoughts on playing time: Keira Scott and Sarah Rambus opening the year as the starting forwards was certainly notable. Rambus scored 12 points in 15 minutes. Scott played 18 minutes, which is one of the higher marks in her Syracuse career . The guard rotation will be something FLJ will likely be sorting out during the early part of the non-con schedule. Tyi Skinner (11 points and 5 assists) and Emely Rodriguez (13 pints on 5/11 shooting) are the clear starting backcourt going forward. Both played around 20 minutes. Monitoring what happens behind them, with Olivia Schmitt, Angelica Velez, Célaine Ricco , and Madison Howard competing for backup minutes. Feeling optimistic about the performances of the transfer forwards, Rambus and Jaleesa Molina (9 points and 6 rebounds in 18 minutes), either of whom can play next to Izoje in the frontcourt. The rookie @celaine_rco shows off her speed 💨 📺 https://t.co/mZBGgptc65 pic.twitter.com/Ocb9CD5Xqe — Syracuse Women's Basketball (@CuseWBB) November 3, 2026 I’m expecting FLJ to give plenty of time and opportunities in Syracuse’s next game against Cornell, which was picked to finish sixth in the Ivy League. The real “bellwether” game for the rotation will likely come against Harvard, a road contest and Syracuse’s last before its three-game stretch in Puerto Rico. Defense remains the Orange’s calling card Opponent context is important to note, but what was discussed in the preseason is still true: defense will be Syracuse’s calling card for the entire season. Outside the second quarter, the Orange held Sacred Heart to 11 points or less in the other three periods and under 28% shooting for the entire contest. They were also plus-19 in points off turnovers, forcing a ridiculous 28 of them. Ricco and Rodriguez combined for 11 steals, and five players had at least two.
