item.title: Bills power rankings: Many outlets put Buffalo at No. 1 as Vikings tumble ahead of MNF in Week 9
item.description: The Buffalo Bills aren’t just sitting atop the NFL power rankings anymore. They’re becoming the nearly unanimous choice. Following their dominant 36-10 victory over the Baltimore Ravens, the Bills (6-1) have claimed the No. 1 spot in seven of the eight national power rankings we track each week. Buffalo entered Week 8 already ranked first by four outlets, but apparently dismantling Baltimore was enough to convince nearly everyone else to get on board. Well, almost everyone. USA Today remains the lone holdout, ranking Buffalo sixth despite the Bills sitting atop the other seven national lists. Meanwhile, Buffalo’s next opponent, the Minnesota Vikings (6-1), is heading in the opposite direction. After suffering their first loss of the season, the Vikings experienced a dramatic fall across all eight outlets. But does one loss really change how dangerous Minnesota is? Let’s take a look. Buffalo Bills: Week 9 power rankings Buffalo’s average ranking improved from 2.38 to 1.63, with seven outlets placing the Bills at the very top of the NFL. That’s a significant shift from last week, when four outlets had Buffalo at the top and the remaining four weren’t quite ready to hand over the crown. Apparently, a 26-point victory over Baltimore helped settle the debate. Well, for everyone except USA Today. To its credit, USA Today did move Buffalo up three spots, from ninth to sixth. But with seven other outlets ranking the Bills first, Nate Davis clearly isn’t ready to join the party. At this point, I’m starting to wonder what Buffalo has to do to crack his top five. Score 50? Win blindfolded? Convince Josh Allen to play defense, too? Kidding. Mostly. Trending up: Buffalo’s defense For much of the season, Buffalo’s defense has faced questions about its ability to consistently pressure quarterbacks, create turnovers, and finish games. Against Baltimore, the Bills answered with four sacks, three takeaways, and just 144 total yards allowed. It’s important to acknowledge that the Ravens lost both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injuries. That certainly affected Baltimore’s offense. But Buffalo still had to execute. The defense capitalized on its opportunities, controlled the game, and delivered the kind of performance that had been missing in several earlier matchups. The question now is whether that momentum carries into Minnesota. Trending down: The margin for error When seven of eight outlets rank you No. 1, there’s really nowhere left to climb. And with that recognition comes a different kind of pressure. The challenge now isn’t getting to No. 1. It’s staying there. Minnesota Vikings: Week 9 power rankings While Buffalo is enjoying life at the top of the rankings, Minnesota is experiencing the other side of the national media’s weekly mood swings. The Vikings entered Week 8 undefeated and ranked No. 1 by two outlets. Following their 19-15 loss to the Detroit Lions, they dropped in every ranking we track. Their average ranking fell from 2.63 to 7.38, a declin

item.title: 7 NFL teams with best chance to win Super Bowl LXI entering Week 9
item.description: Week 8 changed the NFL championship conversation at the line of scrimmage. Chicago’s upgraded front helped dismantle Seattle. Denver finished against Kansas City. Jacksonville crushed Indianapolis, then learned its defense had lost two important starters for the season. Those developments matter beyond the standings. Championship teams need protection, defensive resistance, and another answer when their quarterback cannot supply everything. Winning matters. Whether the winning formula survives better opponents matters more. Now let’s stack’em up. MORE: Bold predictions for Week 9 of 2026 NFL season 7. Cincinnati Bengals Nov 1, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) looks on during warm up prior to the game against the Tennessee Titans at Paycor Stadium. That reveals both the ceiling and the burden. Atlanta in Madrid comes next; Pittsburgh afterward provides a better examination of protection and possession control. Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins can overwhelm playoff coverage. They cannot keep compensating for four giveaways and a defense that allowed a one-win opponent to dictate so much. Cincinnati stays ahead of the teams outside because its passing answers are more dependable. Denver’s defensive safety net earns the edge. 6. Denver Broncos Previous: Unranked | Back in the top seven Denver’s 28-24 comeback against Kansas City supplied something its case needed: meaningful offensive help. Bo Nix and Jonah Coleman created late scoring opportunities before the defense finished the goal-line stand. Carolina comes before the bye, with Pittsburgh and Christmas against Buffalo offering tougher tests of that progress. The front, coaching and defensive depth travel well. JL Skinner’s critical stop while replacing an injured Brandon Jones illustrated the latter. The offense still finished two of 11 on third down, however. Denver returns because its winning formula expanded; it remains sixth because routine offensive efficiency still trails the dramatic finishes. 5. Kansas City Chiefs Oct 18, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) throws a pass during the first quarter against the Los Angeles Chargers at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images Previous: No. 2 | Down 3 Kansas City rediscovered enough offense to lead Denver by 11 in the fourth quarter, then lost 28-24. Eleven penalties for 105 yards helped turn control into another failure. The Jets offer a reset, but Thanksgiving in Buffalo and December trips to the Rams and Bengals will demand cleaner football. Patrick Mahomes, Andy Reid and Steve Spagnuolo still provide a formidable championship foundation, with Kenneth Walker offering another offensive route.

item.title: Thursday Rockpile: What we know about the Rockies competing pitching philosophies
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - MAY 09: Colorado Rockies Pitching Coach Alon Leichman and Assistant Pitching Coach Gabe Ribas during a game against the Philadelphia Phillies at Citizens Bank Park on May 09, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The offseason has barely begun and yet it has already been an eventful one for the Colorado Rockies. On October 15, they fired pitching coach Alon Leichman after just a single year with the team. This past Monday, they hired Ethan Katz as his replacement . On the surface this all seems pretty simple: Leichman, in his first season as a head pitching coach, oversaw a pitching staff that had the worst ERA, the second-worst FIP, and the fifth-worst fWAR in all of MLB. Before his brief foray as the assistant pitching coach for the (barely) playoff-bound Houston Astros, Katz was the Chicago White Sox primary pitching coach for five seasons. When just looking at the basic facts, the Rockies have simply pivoted from a coach whose first results were poor to one with more experience; totally mundane. The drama, however, comes from the details. Some of those details may have come out in the latest edition of the DNVR podcast in which host Christian Saez shared a summary of conversations with both Leichman and unnamed members of the Rockies front office. According to DNVR, the reason for the Rockies moving on from Leichman wasn’t purely results based but instead part of a fundamental inability for Leichman and the other members of the coaching staff to align on a shared vision for Rockies pitching. Last offseason, the newly-appointed Rockies front office took the approach of bringing in the best pitching minds they could find, assuming that a melting pot of different approaches and ideas would lead to the best results. Instead, it appears as though competing ideas simply led to players getting mixed messages over the course of the season. The variety of “experiments” that the Rockies came into the 2026 season attempting to run with their pitching staff ( pitch suggestions from the dugout , heavy use of openers , etc.) were reportedly Leichman-led efforts. Leichman, as quoted on the DNVR podcast, characterized his tenure this way: “I felt like they brought me in and then after the month of May we struggled, they ditched everything that I wanted. I couldn’t get one voice to the players and ultimately paid for it.” According to DNVR, the coaching staff spent a full week after the season attempting to resolve their differences in philosophies and to create a consensus about the path forward. When they were unable to arrive at a resolution, the front office essentially chose which side to move forward with in order to make sure that they had a unified plan in place next season. The odd thing about this, from the outside perspective, is that the Rockies best pitching results in 2026 were very clearly during the early portion of the season when their experimentation was in full

item.title: Stephen A. Smith counters Adam Silver’s 40-minute idea with new NBA solution
item.description: Photo by Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images for SiriusXM Adam Silver might be looking at trimming NBA games to 40 minutes, but Stephen A. Smith has other ideas. With Anthony Edwards and Tyrese Haliburton already missing chunks of time, the league’s health problem is front and center once again. It’s got Adam Silver seriously kicking around the idea of cutting games down to 40 minutes, similar to international ball. The thinking is straightforward, with less floor time means less wear and tear, and fewer stars potentially out on the sidelines. But shaving eight minutes off the clock hasn’t sat well with everyone, resulting in a huge pushback over whether trimming court time actually fixes player durability or just messes with the integrity of the game. Stephen A. Smith wants to eliminate back-to-backs in the NBA Stephen A. Smith wasn’t buying Adam Silver’s 40-minute pitch for a second, with the preference to reduce the amount of back-to-back games instead in the NBA . He said, on his YouTube channel : “I think the priority should be eliminating as many back-to-back games as possible.” NBA teams still face an average of 14.2 back-to-backs during the 2026–27 season, with some playing as many as 16. However, the league has eliminated four-games-in-five-nights stretches from the regular-season schedule. Teams also cannot simply rest their biggest stars whenever they choose. Under the NBA’s Player Participation Policy, teams generally cannot sit two designated star players in the same game without an approved exception. Nationally televised games also receive special protection, with stars generally expected to be available. Exceptions exist for injuries, personal circumstances and approved rest restrictions based on age, career workload or serious injury history. item.title: Ivan Demidov Injury Update Bad News for Montreal Canadiens
item.description: Apr 25, 2025; Montreal, Quebec, CAN; Washington Capitals goalie Logan Thompson (48) makes a save against Montreal Canadiens forward Ivan Demidov (93) during the second period in game three of the first round of the 2025 Stanley Cup Playoffs at the … | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Levi Pike, Editor An Ivan Demidov injury update came from an unexpected source on Wednesday as the player’s agent broke the news on the DFO Insider Podcast with Jeff Marek and David Pagnotta . As the timeline for Demidov’s return from injury has approached, fans and media have been waiting on news from the Montreal Canadiens, but none has been forthcoming. On Wednesday, the update came in an unanticipated manner and the news was not positive. Let’s get into the details. Agent Delivers Bad News Regarding Ivan Demidov Injury On Wednesday, player agent Dan Millstein from Gold Star Hockey appeared on the DFO Insider Podcast. Millstein is the agent for several high profile NHL players, including Ivan Demidov. Marek asked Millstein for an injury status update on Demidov, and Millstein confirmed two details about the Ivan Demidov injury. He said that that Demidov had suffered a fractured ankle during the preseason and that he should be back “in a few weeks”. Demidov had played the first two games of the season with the Montreal Canadiens before it was announced that Demidov had suffered an injury and would be out for two to four weeks. That announcement came on October 6th. Four weeks brought us to this past Tuesday, and now “a few weeks” have been added to that timeline. Sep 22, 2025; Montreal, Quebec, CAN; Montreal Canadiens forward Ivan Demidov (93) plays the puck and Pittsburgh Penguins forward Anthony Mantha (39) defends during the overtime period at the Bell Centre. Mandatory Credit: Eric Bolte-Imagn Images Playing Through Injury Millstein confirmed that even though the injury had happened in the preseason and Demidov’s ankle was bothering him, he kept playing. He said that following the season opener in Toronto, Demidov told him that something was bothering him and didn’t feel right. But then he went out and played a second game. It was after that second game that the Canadiens shut him down. Millstein commented, “Those young kids, they just play through pain.” He said they realized two weeks later that he had an issue that needed medical attention. This has been an area of concern for the Montreal Canadiens, where players have played through injury and it was feared they may have made things worse. The concern resulted in some changes to the medical staff in the summer of 2024. The organization will be watching their prized forward closely to ensure he is healed before he returns, and that the Ivan Demidov injury doesn’t become a bigger issue. Ivan Demidov Injury Impacting Player Development Demidov is in his sophomore season, and expectations were high following a rookie season that saw him score 19 goals and 62 points. item.title: What Ole Miss can replicate from Auburn’s upset of Georgia
item.description: ATHENS, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 17: Gunner Stockton #14 of the Georgia Bulldogs is tackled by Elijah Melendez #9 of the Auburn Tigers during the first quarter at Sanford Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Athens, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The upset of the season so far has been Auburn’s win over then No. 1 Georgia in Athens just weeks ago. No. 10 Ole Miss now hosts No. 2 Georgia in Oxford on Saturday with both teams looking for a win to solidify not only its College Football Playoff chances but to improve its place in the SEC standings. So what in the name of Auburn Jesus happened to have Alex Golesh victorious over Kirby Smart? And does Ole Miss have any way to produce the same results? The biggest number that sticks out from Auburn’s upset win is the turnover margin of +3. The Bulldogs lost a fumble and starting quarterback Gunner Stockton threw two interceptions while the Tigers didn’t register a turnover all game. This isn’t one of those rocket science concepts of the game, but extra possessions even when a team is more talented, at home, playing at night, whatever the circumstances, changes the game. There’s bad news and then there’s more bad news when it comes to making this occur again. First off, the Rebels turnover margin for the season is like the GPA of Bluto in Animal House – zero point zero. Ole Miss hasn’t had much success in generating turnovers (12 thus far) and then it gives the ball away at the exact same rate. The Rebels are more offensively talented than the Tigers, however, so even a +1 for either team on Saturday could be the difference in the game. Which leads to more bad news as Georgia ranks 15th in the nation in turnover margin (+0.75) and the Bulldogs have had only nine turnovers all year. Yes, taking away the Auburn disaster, Georgia has only six turnovers in its other seven football games. You can’t plan on more than maybe one fumble or interception come Saturday. Additionally on the front of creating more possessions, Auburn went 2/2 on fourth down conversions to keep crucial drives alive. Now this is one area where I think Ole Miss is going to have to take some calculated risks against Georgia. Ole Miss is 5/9 on fourth down conversions this season, so it is not as commonplace to see the Rebels roll the dice as it was in previous years. Pete Golding is going to have to pick his moments in this game as both coaches are likely going to play a more conservative style given the implications for the winner. Keeping the drives alive and keeping Georgia on the field will be a must have for the Rebels offense. Lastly, Auburn’s offensive attack was not overwhelming when it shocked the college football world, but it was very balanced. The Tigers rushed for 192 yards and passed for 174 yards, and its talented and mobile QB Byrum Brown led both of those attacks. Does this sound like something Trinidad Chambliss can do? item.title: 5 things we learned about the Browns in the Steelers loss
item.description: The Cleveland Browns compiled a 5-2-0 record before meeting the Pittsburgh Steelers for the second time this season. Despite beating the Steelers 27-24 in Cleveland in Week 4, the Browns were taken to the woodshed in the rubber game by losing 27-6 . The game pitted two teams that had identical records and were tied for the AFC North Division lead. Now, Pittsburgh sits atop the division all alone, while the Browns are now situated in third place after the Cincinnati Bengals defeated the Tennessee Titans to grab second place. RELATED: RUN DEFENSE IS SCARY What did the Steelers’ loss teach the Browns’ fanbase ? Their coaching staff? The front office? Here are five things likely learned: The Browns will not be giving QB Deshaun Watson a contract extension Cleveland’s coaching staff has not hinted at benching Watson for the season. He has been a roller coaster and just isn’t any degree of the elite signal-caller he once was with Clemson and the Houston Texans. And now, he is on concussion protocol, which means he will have to sit out at least one game. This year is Watson’s first without getting injured while playing for the Browns; then he was placed in concussion protocol on Wednesday . To date, he hasn’t completed a full season despite being a roster member since 2022. He has missed a total of 57 games. Realistically, he has had only two great games with Cleveland: Week 10 in the 33-31 win over the Baltimore Ravens in 2023, and the Week 7 27-24 victory over the Titans this year. Watson has had a few good games this year with exceptional completion percentages in several games, including 80.0% (Bucs), 72.7% (Jaguars and Steelers first game), and 69.4% (Titans). All five triumphs in the win column this year were orchestrated by a comeback win by Watson. There were rumblings that perhaps if the Browns made the postseason, the front office should re-sign him to an extension and keep him going forward. Those thoughts were questioned when Cleveland lost to a lesser team, the New York Jets. In that contest, Watson had a 45.5% completion rate and struggled against a defense that challenged a clean pocket. The Steelers this past weekend used that blueprint and made Watson appear minimal on passing downs. They exposed Watson’s inability to get to safety once the pocket walls began to crumble. Pittsburgh also showed that Watson could not finish drives, especially when the drive concluded in the Red Zone. After the first quarter, Watson was 1 for 2 for three yards passing and no points on the board. At the half, he was 9 for 13 for 107 yards, was sacked four times, and his offense had just two field goals. To put an exclamation mark on sub-par play, Cleveland failed to score any points in the second half. Despite Watson being mentioned for the league “Comeback Player of the Year,” those views have now dissipated. item.title: When was the last time Lazio led the Serie A table?
item.description: When was the last time Lazio led the Serie A table? Lazio have surprisingly jumped to the top of the Serie A table after the first ten rounds, but when was the last time they achieved such a feat? Gennaro Gattuso’s Lazio have shocked online casino users this season, as the Biancocelesti lead Serie A with 28 points. They’ve won nine matches and drawn once, earning a three-point lead over defending champions Inter. Over the weekend, Lazio beat Cagliari 2-1, while Inter lost the derby della Madonnina 3-1 to city rivals Milan. ROME, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: SS Lazio Gennaro Gattuso celebrates after goal during the Serie A match between SS Lazio and Cagliari Calcio at Stadio Olimpico on November 01, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images) Lazio came back from one-goal down in their most recent game against Cagliari to claim a 2-1 victory. “Those who came on showed great determination, hunger and vehemence; they changed the game,” Gattuso said at full-time. “That is big for a coach to see. Not starting will always irritate a player, but the five substitutions made the difference today, and that makes me proud.” As Tancredi Palmieri reported on X, this is the first time in 16 years Lazio sit alone at the top of the table. “We are all up there; we still need 12 points to achieve the target of 40 that we set at the start of the season. Every team in the league is balanced and well-structured, so we’ve got to keep taking it one game at a time and see where we end up,” Gattuso added. ROME, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: SS Lazio head coach Gennaro Gattuso during the Serie A match between SS Lazio and Cagliari Calcio at Stadio Olimpico on November 01, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images) “It is best that we don’t look at the table right now, or it’ll make us dizzy. We’ve got to push hard, rest, then push hard again.” Edy Reja was the last Lazio coach to top the standings. Ironically, that also happened after Round 10 in the 2010-11 campaign. This marks Lazio ‘s third-longest wait between spells at the top of the table. The club had previously endured two even longer droughts: 25 years from 1974 to 1999 and 36 years from 1936 to 1972. Gattuso’s feat is even more surprising because the team started the season with low expectations. The Biancocelesti were knocked out of the Coppa Italia first round in August, losing 2-0 at home to Serie B side Mantova. ROME, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Fisayo Dele-Bashiru and Andrea Pinamonti of S.S. Lazio celebrate after the Serie A match between SS Lazio and Cagliari Calcio at Stadio Olimpico on November 01, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) Furthermore, fans are boycotting every home match to protest owner Claudio Lotito, yet the team is pulling off a fantastic effort, remaining unbeaten in the opening ten games of the campaign and reaching the top of the standings, something few would have imagined just a few weeks ago. item.title: New hoax bomb threats hit European flights
item.description: Italian, French and Bulgarian fighter jets scrambled Thursday as about 20 flights were hit by a third day of hoax bomb alerts across Europe, authorities and airlines said. The hoaxes involved flights from Greece to Britain, but particularly targeted low-cost carriers and flights to or from Bulgaria, Czech Republic and Italy. Three flights were diverted but all the jets landed safely with no explosives found. No claim of responsibility was made for all the flights, but a threat against two flights sent to airports in Rome and published by an Italian newspaper contained misogynistic messages. – Under escort, diversions – At least five flights received an air force escort after receiving bomb threats. Bulgaria’s air force escorted three Ryanair planes headed for Sofia from Madrid, Copenhagen, and London Stansted. All three planes were inspected and no explosives found, an interior ministry spokesperson told AFP. French fighters accompanied an Aer Lingus flight from Dublin that was headed to Rome, diverting it to the Evreux military base 100 kilometers (60 miles) west of Paris. Other jets were also diverted. The Ryanair flight from London-Stansted to Sofia was diverted to Plovdiv Airport, east of the capital, while a Wizz Air flight from Milan to Warsaw was re-routed to Vienna, the airlines said. – Who and why – Italian newspaper Il Corriere della Sera published the text of a message sent to ADR, the company that manages Rome’s airports. A company source confirmed the report to AFP. “You are all accomplices in a criminal conspiracy, and for this we want to annihilate you. Right now explosive devices have been placed on the following flights: AY1751 Helsinki–Rome and EI402 Dublin–Rome,” read the message, with media noting it was written in “broken Italian”. “We Male State fighters with our actions today will leave a mark in history. Your feminist regime will remember it forever. The explosion will occur in 60 minutes. Today your sky will be red,” read the text. There is a far-right movement in Russia called the Male State, but AFP could not confirm any link to the message. Prague Airport spokeswoman Denisa Hejtmankova told AFP the airport had received threats in emails from anonymous addresses. The EU’s transport commissioner, Apostolos Tzitzikostas, wrote on X that it was “too early to draw conclusions on whether the reported incidents are linked.” But European authorities say there has been rise in hybrid attacks, sometimes linked to Russia or Iran. – Landing safely – Most of the flights targeted Thursday landed without incident at their original destinations. Those included a Lot Polish Airlines flight from Warsaw to Brussels and a Wizz Air flight from Milan to Bucharest. In the Czech Republic, four targeted planes bound for Prague flown by Ryanair, Easy Jet and Sky Express all landed safely. “We perceive the credibility of the threats as low,” said Czech police on X. “Nevertheless, we are not underestimating the situation, and all necessary securi

item.title: NISO blames gas shortages, low water levels for drop in power generation
item.description: The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) has attributed the decline in electricity generation on the national grid to gas supply constraints affecting thermal power plants and reduced water levels at hydroelectric power stations. The operator disclosed this in a statement on Thursday, explaining that the constraints had reduced available generation and affected electricity allocations to Distribution Companies (DisCos). According to NISO, inadequate gas supply has limited the capacity of affected thermal generating plants to operate at their available levels, while reduced water inflows into reservoirs have weakened output from hydroelectric stations. It said the shortfall had affected the volume of electricity allocated to DisCos for distribution to consumers, resulting in shorter hours of supply and increased load shedding across distribution networks. NISO noted that the extent of the impact varied across distribution companies, depending on available generation and their respective electricity allocations. The operator acknowledged the difficulties faced by electricity consumers nationwide, expressing appreciation for the concerns raised by members of the public and other stakeholders. It said efforts were ongoing to diversify the energy mix of the national grid to strengthen electricity supply security and reduce exposure to prevailing operational constraints. NISO reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining grid stability, optimising the dispatch of available electricity generation and ensuring the secure, reliable and efficient operation of the national grid. The post NISO blames gas shortages, low water levels for drop in power generation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Raphinha extends Barcelona deal by two years
item.description: Captain Raphinha has signed a contract extension until 2030, La Liga champions Barcelona said on Thursday. The 29-year-old Brazilian forward, who joined the Catalan giants in 2022, had been contracted until 2028. “A declaration of intent. Our dear captain will continue to lead our project until 2030,” Barca wrote in a statement. Raphinha said in September that he wanted to extend his deal, and maybe even end his career at Barca. He has been in the form of his life this season, scoring 19 goals and contributing three assists in 13 matches in all competitions. The former Leeds United winger took over the captaincy at the start of the season following the departures of Ronald Araujo and Marc-Andre ter Stegen. He has also shifted inside from his usual position on the wing to fill the gap created by strikers Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres leaving the club. He has been Barca’s most potent forward since German Hansi Flick took over in 2024, leading Barca to back-to-back La Liga crowns. item.title: Tinubu gets opposition backing in Ekiti, Oyebanji pledges 90% votes
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela Ado-Ekiti — President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign received a boost in Ekiti State on Thursday as governorship candidates of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Social Democratic Party (SDP) and Allied Peoples Movement (APM) in the June 20 election declared support for his second-term bid. The opposition candidates announced their support at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ado-Ekiti, where Governor Biodun Oyebanji also pledged that the state would deliver at least 90 per cent of its votes for Tinubu in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who represented the President at the rally, said the support of the former opposition candidates, former governors and other political leaders demonstrated the APC’s growing political strength in the state. He urged Ekiti residents to improve on the 201,495 votes recorded by Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, when the APC won in all 16 local government areas of the state. Shettima recalled that Oyebanji secured 85.74 per cent of the votes in the June governorship election, expressing optimism that the APC would increase its performance in the presidential poll. He said the Federal Government had taken difficult decisions to address the country’s economic challenges and that the benefits of the reforms were beginning to emerge. “With a total registered vote of 1,028,000, it is our hope, prayer and aspiration that from January 16, 2027, APC will garner 90 to 95 per cent of the votes cast in Ekiti State,” he said. In his remarks, Oyebanji described the rally as a demonstration of political unity in Ekiti, saying the endorsement by former opposition candidates and political leaders had strengthened the APC ahead of the presidential election. He recalled that Tinubu, during his 2022 campaign, had urged Ekiti residents to vote for both him and Oyebanji, promising federal support for the state if elected. According to the governor, the President has fulfilled that promise through what he described as unprecedented federal support for Ekiti since its creation 30 years ago. Oyebanji said the APC’s 85.7 per cent performance in the June governorship election reflected residents’ satisfaction with his administration and the Federal Government’s interventions. He added that the state was determined to improve on its previous electoral performance and deliver not less than 90 per cent of its votes for Tinubu. Also speaking, the Director-General of the campaign, Abdulaziz Yari, urged Ekiti residents to deliver at least 800,000 votes for the President, representing about 90 per cent of the state’s votes. Yari said Tinubu had supported the state through investments in education, road construction, youth development and women’s empowerment, urging residents to reciprocate through their votes. item.title: Can 142m Nigerian youths change 2027 elections narrative?
item.description: By Gabriel Ewepu Nigerian youths constitute a significant portion of the country’s population at over 142 million. Also, recently the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, disclosed that over 9.32 million young Nigerians registered in the 2026 Continuous Voter Registration, CVR, exercise. These numbers has made expectations mount over young Nigerians’ potential influence on the 2027 general elections. Read Also: Court sacks Mark-led ADC exco, voids Atiku’s candidacy However, despite their numerical strength and growing political awareness, questions remain whether they can translate their numbers into decisive electoral power. While some stakeholders believe Nigerian youths are increasingly politically conscious, determined to challenge the status quo and demand accountability, others argue that voter apathy, declining confidence in the electoral process, political manipulations and weak grassroots structures could undermine their participation. Consequently, the debate has shifted beyond whether Nigerian youths are ready to vote to whether they are sufficiently organised, motivated and confident in the electoral system to shape electoral outcomes and hold political leaders accountable. Against this backdrop, stakeholders who spoke on the readiness of Nigerian youths ahead of the 2027 elections offered divergent perspectives. They highlighted the opportunities, frustrations and challenges confronting the country’s youthful population. Nigerian youths are losing hope in elections – Olanrewaju Jerry Tobi Olanrewaju, is ‘The Chief Farmer of Africa’, and Founder and Team Lead, Jet Farms and Agro Solutions Limited, based in Abuja. He asserted that most Nigerian youths are losing hope in exercising their franchise as eligible voters. Olanrewaju said: “Honestly, I was hopeful. But over time, many young Nigerians, particularly young farmers, have begun to lose hope. Many of the farmers I work with cannot even feel the impact of the government’s Renewed Hope Agenda. While some macroeconomic indicators may suggest progress, the reality on the farms tells a different story. “The rising cost of inputs, high transportation costs, limited access to affordable financing, and unstable markets have made farming increasingly difficult. “Many young people who once saw agriculture as an opportunity are now afraid to farm because they are uncertain about their survival and returns on investment.” In his counsel he said, “As we approach 2027, Nigerian youths must move beyond social media conversations and become intentional about shaping the elections. “However, their participation must be driven by issues, accountability, credible leadership, and policies that address their everyday realities.” Nigerian youths tired of manipulation, ready to change narrative – Donald Abareowei Benaembele Donald is a vibrant youth leader in Bayelsa State and also the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Gologolo Global Views Enterprise. item.title: France Workers Strike, March For ‘Dignified Wage’
item.description: Striking workers marched across France against the rising cost of living on Thursday, with hundreds of thousands of people expected to take to the streets nationwide in a new escalation following weeks of protest. More than 250,000 people were taking part in demonstrations across 73 cities by the afternoon, the major labour union CGT said. The demonstrations come as the eurozone’s second largest economy battles to redress its finances, six months ahead of elections to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with the far right leading in opinion polls. The high school student movement that began with youths protesting over learning conditions has coincided with widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality, which culminated on October 17 in the worst rioting France has seen in years. Sylvie Larneury, 61, a healthcare manager, and her 61-year-old partner, an IT specialist, were on strike Thursday so they could join the march in the central city of Clermont-Ferrand. “We’re fed up. We’re not starving, but we have to help our children even though they’ve studied,” she said. “We’ve had enough of social injustice,” she added, criticising what she called “a repressive government that defends its own interests and not those of the majority”. The unions are calling for across-the-board wage raises, tax reforms and better learning conditions for young people and have complained about police restrictions on certain protests. Protesters take part in a demonstration as part of a nationwide day of actions as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks in Bordeaux on November 5, 2026. Photo by CHRISTOPHE ARCHAMBAULT / AFP Protesting in the city of Lyon, winegrower Martin Thiberge said he wanted to take part in demonstrations he saw as drawing together people from across French society. “We want to make a living from our work, to make a dignified wage,” he said. As many as 80,000 people were expected to march from 2:00 pm (1300 GMT) in the capital Paris. The planned action prompted the Eiffel Tower to close for the day, operators said on the monument’s website. School blockades Dozens of high-schoolers protested in several cities, with the government reporting blockades at 81 out of the country’s 3,700 high schools. A high school student association said classes had been suspended at 1,000 such secondary schools, including those blockaded and those closed on a day of strikes. Around 16 percent of teachers nationwide were on strike, the education ministry said. In Paris, police used tear gas to try to prevent students from blocking access to the Helene-Boucher high school, an AFP reporter said. French police officers march amid the smoke during a demonstration as part of a nationwide day of actions as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks, in Nantes on November 5, 2026. item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Tinubu The ruling All Progressives Congress APC has set a target of 800,000 votes in Ekiti State for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, with the Director General of its Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Senator Abdul’aziz Yari, assuring that Northern Nigeria “is ready for Asiwaju 2027” and “is going to deliver him from A to Z.” Yari spoke on Thursday at the party’s campaign rally in Ado-Ekiti, where he asked the state to improve on the roughly 80 per cent it gave Tinubu in 2022. “Out of 1,080,000 votes, and PVC collected over 900,000, this is my request, and by extension, of course, of the President to you. We are looking for 800,000 votes, representing about 90 per cent,” he said. He told the gathering that the state governor had earlier given a breakdown of the Tinubu administration’s achievements and said the president “did not forget Ekiti”, citing schools, universities, roads, education support for youths and women empowerment. Yari said the candidates of the Peoples Democratic Party PDP, the Allied Peoples Movement APM and the Social Democratic Party SDP who contested the last governorship election against the governor were at the rally “to show solidarity, their togetherness with the Governor when it comes to Bola Ahmed Tinubu in 2027.” He added that the reward for a heavy turnout would be more federal presence in the state. “The President promised to do more for the Ekiti people,” he said. Turning to the North, Yari said, “We in Northern Nigeria, Bola, are more of us than you in Ekiti, than you in Ondo, than you in Oyo, than you in Osun, than you in Lagos. Bola Ahmed supported our children and supported our people to become number one citizens in this country up to three times. So, we in the north, we are ready for Asiwaju 2027, and we are going to deliver him from A to Z.” The PCC boss also challenged the opposition to say what it would do differently. “What are they going to do differently than what we are having today? Government brings down the inflation,” he said. “As we promised Nigerians, we are going to campaign with our numbers, with what we have done for Nigerians. We are not AI product people. We are saying the truth, and we are asking to go and take that truth. “All the numbers are there, ranging from inflation, ranging from exchange rates, and ranging from balance of trade. All of them are there for anyone to go and take. If they have answers, we are waiting for their answers,” he added. The National Chairman of the APC, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, said his role at the rally was to present the party’s candidates, “starting from the President down to the National Assembly to the House of Assembly candidates in Ekiti state.” Yilwatda pointed to road projects in the state, some of them ongoing and some completed by the president. “We have a road from here to Akure constructed by Mr President. Our governor was elected on the basis of his performance. So also was the President,” he said. H

item.description: The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Minister, Nyesom Wike, has explained the many reasons Nigerians should re-elect President Bola Tinubu in the upcoming 2027 general elections. The FCT Minister spoke on Wednesday during his monthly ministerial press briefing in Port Harcourt on Thursday. Wike said he enjoyed his job as FCT Minister and remained committed to it. “I enjoy my job as FCT Minister, and I’m committed to it. Yes, I have pressure to deliver, but positively,” he said. Wike also said Ogoni people had benefited from empowerment under the President. “Ogoni people have been looking for empowerment, and now President Tinubu has done a lot of empowerment for them. If you tell them not to vote for Mr President, they’ll look at you like you’re not okay,” he said. He insisted that “no government has done more in the fight against insecurity than this government.” The former Rivers State governor responded to critics and political rivals, including the Turaki-led PDP faction, Imo State Governor Hope Uzodinma, and the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), University of Abuja branch. FCT Minister Nyesom Wike Addressing Amaechi’s candidacy on the platform of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Wike questioned the former governor’s record in Rivers State. “Why will Rivers people support a former governor who can’t explain the issue of 14billion earmarked for fumigating the state? Up till now I still have mosquito bites,” he said. He added: “You budgeted $39m to construct a general hospital and up till now we can’t find any hospital. How can I support such a person? He sold out gas turbine, so what’s the impact of his leadership on Rivers people?” Wike further alleged that Amaechi contracted a Ghanaian to plant trees along Aba Road for N8bn. “My brother, it was terrible! I don’t want to waste my energy. His candidacy is dead on arrival,” he said. On Amaechi’s electoral pull, Wike said: “Amaechi was a former super minister; he didn’t get 15% in Rivers State. Reacting to Amaechi’s reported remark about divorcing his wife if she supported Tinubu, Wike asked: “Why does he have to bring his wife into politics? Last time he brought in his mother. item.title: Microsoft fixed Excel 2016 copy-paste bug. Then reintroduced it. Now it's fixed again
item.description: The Excel copy-and-paste bug is back, which means Microsoft is making a second round of fixes. The bug first appeared in the September update and manifested in multiple versions of Excel as a silent failure of the paste operation. Users copied content and attempted to paste it, but the destination cell was unchanged no matter how hard they mashed the Ctrl+V keys. Microsoft fixed it in mid-September. But it made a comeback in Excel 2016 when users installed October's security update . Microsoft has now released a new build of Excel 2016 to address the reintroduction of the bug: build 16.0.5574.1006. The company wrote: "The new build includes all security updates for Microsoft Excel 2016, and also fixes the issue that was reintroduced in 16.0.5574.1005, in which paste operations might fail if the workbook contains conditional formatting." Microsoft did not explain how the bug slipped back in. Copy and paste is, after all, a niche bit of functionality. Users reported the recurrence of the bug in October after the KB5002934 update was applied. Rolling back the update resolved the problem until Windows Update pushed the patch again. KB5002934 is a security update that resolves glitches including remote code execution and information disclosure vulnerabilities. The problem affects only Excel 2016 and is not the result of the latest Windows security update. Rather, it was reintroduced in an Excel update delivered through Windows Update. A user in a Microsoft Excel forum said the issue had appeared on workstations throughout their organization. "What's frustrating is that this is the same issue we encountered before, which was supposedly fixed in a previous update. Now it's back, barely a few weeks later." And now, at least, it appears to be fixed once again. Still, if Microsoft is determined to reintroduce bugs into Excel, perhaps it might also be tempted to bring back the Hall of Tortured Souls (a secret first-person 3D mini-game hidden inside Microsoft Excel for Windows 95) and populate it with the testers who managed to miss the issue's resurrection. ®

item.title: NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins is the 1st Black woman to command a space mission. Will we see more diversity in the future on the final frontier?
item.description: null When Jessica Watkins became commander of her mission to the International Space Station, she didn't just fulfill her duty as an astronaut — she made history. Watkins is commanding SpaceX's Crew-13 mission , which launched her and three other astronauts to the I nternational Space Station on Oct. 1. As their Crew Dragon capsule lifted off atop a Falcon 9 rocket that day, Watkins became the first Black woman to command a crewed mission to space. Spaceflight and space science are historically white and male-dominated fields, so this milestone carries incredible significance. "This is certainly an important milestone, I think both for our agency and for the country," Watkins said in a press briefing ahead of Crew-13's launch. This is Watkins' second spaceflight. She previously flew on SpaceX's Crew-4 mission in 2022 and has spent more than 200 days in space to date, though that number will keep climbing for a while, as Crew-13 is set to be an approximately six-month mission. A geologist, astronaut, aquanaut and former professional rugby player, Watkins brings an incredible variety of skills to her new role as mission commander. And, in addition to what she's bringing to her colleagues on mission, she's also providing some serious inspiration for those back on Earth. NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins floats in the International Space Station’s cupola during the Crew-4 mission in this photo, which NASA shared on May 9, 2022. (Image credit: NASA) "Jessica is an inspirational symbol to a lot of people," commercial astronaut and fellow geologist Sian Proctor , who became the first Black woman to pilot a spacecraft on SpaceX's private Inspiration4 mission to orbit in September 2021, told Space.com . Sian shared that the two even crossed paths years ago, when their astronaut training aligned. "It just means so much to so many people when you see a diverse crew, and particularly women, and women of color, in leadership positions," Proctor said. "And it means something for America." The visibility of Watkins' accomplishments and missions carries significant cultural weight. However, in addition to recognizing her many achievements, "you also should celebrate the fact that she's African American and a role model for her community," Proctor said. Sian Proctor from aboard the SpaceX Dragon capsule during the Inspiration4 mission. (Image credit: Tripadvisor) Proctor, who similarly made spaceflight history with her mission, sees Watkins' role in Crew-13 as potentially more than just an exciting moment. Hopefully, she said, it will help lay the foundation for a more diverse future in human spaceflight . "When they announced Jessica, I was super excited because it shows progress," Proctor said, sharing that she finds incredible importance in the "idea of looking at your crew and recognizing the fact that diversity makes the crew stronger." item.title: Tether and Tron Quietly Scrapped T3 Crime Unit Two Months Before $6.3 Billion Binance Hack
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Tether and Tron Quietly Scrapped T3 Crime Unit Two Months Before $6.3 Billion Binance Hack The T3 Financial Crime Unit, the anti-crime alliance Tron, Tether and TRM Labs launched in 2024 and later expanded to Binance, quietly shut down in late August, Bloomberg reported Wednesday, about two months before the record Binance hack. The alliance broke down over the past year amid slow response times and a lack of coordination among its members, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. One of them said T3 was terminated in late August. None of the companies announced the shutdown at the time. Tron, Tether and TRM confirmed that the initiative had wound down, without commenting on the details of the report. Binance declined to comment. “While the very successful T3 program has concluded, Tron remains committed to working to help stop illicit activities on the blockchain, in partnership with law enforcement,” a Tron DAO spokesperson said to Bloomberg . The spokesperson said Tron will share details of a new anti-crime initiative later. A Tether spokesperson said the company will keep working with TRM to disrupt illicit funds and has been taking part in Beacon Network, a real-time intelligence-sharing network TRM launched in August 2025. Tether is also working on the Financial Access and Systemic Empowerment Foundation, or FASE Foundation, which CEO Paolo Ardoino unveiled on X on Oct. 31. TRM’s global head of policy and government affairs, Ari Redbord, said “T3 achieved extraordinary things” and that “Beacon Network builds on that work.” What T3 was built to do Tron, Tether and TRM set up T3 in September 2024 as a public-private unit aimed at illicit use of Tether’s USDT stablecoin on the Tron blockchain. The pitch was speed. TRM supplied blockchain intelligence, Tron supplied network visibility and Tether supplied the power to freeze tokens at the issuer level. The unit said in August 2025 that it had frozen more than $250 million in illicit assets in less than a year. At the same time, it launched T3+, a program for outside partners, with Binance as its first member. Its first joint effort with the exchange froze almost $6 million tied to a pig-butchering scam. The totals kept climbing. TRM put the T3 tally above $300 million in February, when it announced a $70 million Series C round. In May, the unit announced that it had frozen more than $450 million and was working with authorities in 23 jurisdictions on five continents, including the U.S., Spain, Germany, Brazil and the U.K. That May release also said the unit had frozen funds within 24 hours of law enforcement requests in account takeovers and violent crime emergencies. It made no mention of the coordination problems Bloomberg has now described. TRM wrote that the Financial Action Task Force cited T3 in November 2025 guidance as a leading model for public-private enforcement work. item.title: Riot (RIOT) Names Anthropic as Tenant in $28 Billion Texas Lease, Could Owe It 12% Interest
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Riot (RIOT) Names Anthropic as Tenant in $28 Billion Texas Lease, Could Owe It 12% Interest Riot Platforms’ unnamed “Frontier AI Lab” is Anthropic, the bitcoin miner disclosed in its quarterly report filed Wednesday, naming the Claude developer as the tenant behind a 15-year lease worth about $28 billion on its Corsicana, Texas campus. The company’s results release on the same day described the tenant only as a “leading Frontier AI Lab.” The 10-Q is more specific. It says a Riot subsidiary signed the lease on Oct. 28 “with Anthropic PBC (the ‘Frontier AI Lab’),” and the deal became binding on Nov. 4 after Riot’s board approved it and outside consultants signed off on the technical specifications. The filing uses the same defined term for the tenant of Riot’s 191 MW Rockdale lease, signed in August. That makes Anthropic the counterparty on 1,101 MW of the 1,151 MW Riot has contracted. AMD holds the other 50 MW. The Corsicana lease covers 910 MW of critical IT capacity across the whole campus. Base rent starts at $130 per kilowatt per month and rises 3% a year. At that starting rate, the full 910 MW would bring in about $1.42 billion a year. Riot puts average annual rent at about $1.8 billion over the initial term, or roughly $54 billion in total if Anthropic exercises both five-year extensions. Riot’s 12% clause The detail drawing attention sits in the financing terms. The infrastructure company agreed to reimburse Anthropic up to $4 million per megawatt for the data center modules the tenant installs, or up to about $3.6 billion across the full 910 MW. That reimbursement depends on Riot raising money “on market terms reasonably acceptable to it.” If that financing is not available, the 10-Q says , Riot will instead give Anthropic rent credits that amortize the amount “plus interest at 12% per year” over the rest of the initial term. In that case, Anthropic would effectively finance the build itself and recover the cost out of rent at a double-digit rate. Riot’s base case is different. The company expects to fund the reimbursements with non-recourse project debt sized to the contracted rent, and it puts the total capital requirement at about $6 million per MW, or $5.5 billion. It said it does not currently expect to issue equity for the project. Deadlines and exits favor the tenant The lease puts most of the delivery risk on Riot. Capacity arrives in three phases: 400 MW with a first block targeted for June 28, 2027, 200 MW starting Dec. 24, 2027 and 310 MW on July 30, 2028. If Riot delivers more than 60 days late, Anthropic earns escalating rent credits capped at 270 days of base rent for the undelivered blocks. If a phase is not delivered within 270 days of its target, Anthropic can terminate the lease for that phase on 30 days’ notice, with extensions for force majeure of up to 365 days. Riot cannot curtail Anthropic’s power load or enroll the site in voluntary demand response programs without consent, a notable limit for a com

item.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $79,600 as Oil Rebounds and Bank of England Hikes Rates
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $79,600 as Oil Rebounds and Bank of England Hikes Rates Bitcoin price traded near $79,600 on Thursday morning, up about 2% from a day earlier but roughly $21,900 below its price one year ago, after slipping back under $80,000 as oil prices recovered and the Bank of England raised interest rates, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. Bitcoin changed hands at $79,632 at 8:05 a.m. ET, with a market cap of about $1.60 trillion and roughly $35.2 billion in trading volume over the past day. The move gives back a slice of Wednesday’s rally. Bitcoin price held near $80,000 through Wednesday afternoon and stayed above that level overnight, peaking just under $80,900 around 5 p.m. ET. It dipped below $80,000 in the 7 a.m. ET hour on Thursday, as stock futures turned mixed and oil firmed. The pullback is small next to the week’s swing. Bitcoin sat near $75,600 on election night, so Thursday’s price is still more than 5% above that low. Oil and rates set the tone Oil drove Wednesday’s relief rally, and it is now taking some of that back. Brent crude futures rose $1.53, or 1.6%, to $96.15 a barrel on Thursday, while West Texas Intermediate added 52 cents to $88.64. Both benchmarks fell more than 8% on Wednesday to settle at their lowest since Aug. 31. “The situation in the Middle East is still unresolved and that’s why there is some modest recovery in prices at the moment,” UBS commodity analyst Giovanni Staunovo said . That matters for the bitcoin price because energy has been the main channel from the Iran war into inflation and interest rates. Cheaper crude eases pressure on the Federal Reserve. A rebound does the opposite. The Bank of England made that link explicit on Thursday. Its Monetary Policy Committee voted 8-1 to raise Bank Rate by a quarter point to 4%, its first hike in more than three years, with the one dissenter, Catherine Mann, pushing for a half-point move. The bank said U.K. inflation is now expected to rise to around 5% by the middle of next year, citing energy prices tied to a conflict “now in its ninth month.” CNBC called it the last major central bank to start tightening since the war began, a reminder that global rates are still moving against risk assets. Stocks cool, ETFs return U.S. stock futures split Thursday morning after the Dow’s best session since April 2025. Dow futures rose 0.5% and S&P 500 futures added 0.1%, while Nasdaq-100 futures dropped about 0.5% as chip and data center stocks stayed under pressure. Fund demand picked up. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs took in a net $74.6 million on Wednesday, ending a three-session run of outflows that totaled about $1.16 billion. Fidelity’s FBTC drew $236.7 million, more than offsetting a $201.2 million outflow from BlackRock’s IBIT. Supply from miners remains a weight. item.title: 2027: APC chairman seeks Ekiti voters’ support for Tinubu
item.description: National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, has urged voters in Ekiti State to support President Bola Tinubu and other party candidates in the 2027 general elections, citing the administration’s economic reforms and development projects. Yilwatda made the appeal on Thursday at the APC presidential campaign rally in Ado-Ekiti, where he joined Vice President Kashim Shettima, members of the party’s National Working Committee, governors and other stakeholders to present the party’s candidates to voters. In a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media and Information Strategy, Abimbola Tooki, the APC chairman expressed satisfaction with the turnout at the rally, describing it as a demonstration of support for the party and its Renewed Hope Agenda. He said the rally provided an opportunity to present the party’s candidates, including Tinubu and those seeking election into the National Assembly and Ekiti State House of Assembly. Yilwatda described Tinubu as a performer and reformer, saying his administration had introduced policies aimed at repositioning the economy, strengthening public institutions and creating opportunities for Nigerians. He particularly highlighted the administration’s tax reforms, arguing that the new framework was designed to protect low-income earners and small businesses from excessive tax burdens. The APC chairman also cited the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) as an intervention to expand access to higher education, noting that eligible beneficiaries receive a monthly upkeep allowance of N20,000. On infrastructure, he highlighted federal road projects in Ekiti State, including major connections between Ado-Ekiti and Akure, as evidence of the administration’s commitment to improving transportation and economic activities. He urged voters to elect APC candidates across all elective positions, particularly in the National Assembly and state legislature, arguing that their presence would facilitate the implementation of the President’s development agenda. Yilwatda also called on party members and stakeholders in Ekiti to remain united and mobilised ahead of the elections. He expressed confidence that the APC would consolidate its political strength in 2027 and urged Nigerians to renew their support for Tinubu and the party. FCCPC seals firms as oil, salt samples fail fortification tests
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) has sealed manufacturing facilities of defaulting food companies following a survey that revealed inadequate fortification of some vegetable oil and salt products sold in Nigerian markets. The commission also warned food manufacturers to comply with national micronutrient fortification standards, vowing to intensify enforcement against businesses that fail to meet statutory requirements. Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the FCCPC, Tunji Bello, disclosed this on Thursday while presenting the findings of a two-month market survey conducted in partnership with the Global Alliance for Improved Nutrition (GAIN). The survey examined 200 randomly selected samples, comprising 100 vegetable oil and 100 salt products collected from households and open markets across Northern and Southern Nigeria. Laboratory analysis showed that 12 per cent of the vegetable oil samples and two per cent of the salt samples were inadequately fortified with essential micronutrients at the household level. According to Bello, the survey covered both branded and unbranded products. Of the 100 vegetable oil samples, 49 were unbranded, while 51 were branded products, including Devon King’s, Power Oil, Activa, Golden Penny, Laziz, Mamador and Golden Terra, among others. Similarly, 19 of the 100 salt samples were unbranded, while 81 were branded products, comprising 71 samples of Mr Chef and 10 of Dangote salt. The investigation also identified significant gaps in the adoption of digital traceability systems designed to monitor the quality of fortified food products from manufacturing facilities to retail outlets. Bello said the survey used GAIN’s Digital Fortification Quality Traceability Plus (DFQT+) platform to track compliance and promote transparency across the food supply chain. However, regulatory data showed that only six vegetable oil manufacturers had registered on the platform, while just three companies uploaded a combined eight product test results out of the 100 oil samples analysed. He stressed that large-scale food fortification was a mandatory public health policy designed to address micronutrient deficiencies by requiring food processors to enrich staple products with essential nutrients, including vitamin A, iron, folic acid, zinc and iodine. He said the policy was particularly important in tackling hidden hunger and nutritional deficiencies among young children and women of reproductive age. “Consumers must be able to trust the quality of the products they buy and the health benefits those products are advertised to provide. “Consumer protection goes beyond resolving everyday complaints or halting deceptive business practices. It fundamentally comes down to ensuring that citizens are not denied the essential value, safety and nutritional benefits they pay for in the marketplace,” Bello said. item.title: NASA announces experimental X-70 Fractal aircraft: A 'new beginning for aeronautics'
item.description: null NASA has revealed a glimpse of its next X-plane, known as the X-70 Fractal. Or at least what it thinks the X-70 will look like once built. The agency released a short statement on Wednesday (Nov. 4) announcing the X-plane , or experimental plane, declaring it to be a highly maneuverable test bed with a "rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology," allowing NASA to swap both external and internal components on-the-fly. This modular architecture will allow NASA to "explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight," according to the agency's statement . The announcement was made alongside an AI-generated image showing two canted vertical tail fins emerging from swirling smoke. Little can be gleaned from the image about what final form the X-70 might take, but the tail fins are somewhat reminiscent of the Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor or Boeing F/A-18 Super Hornet . "The X-70 Fractal gives NASA a crewed, high-performance platform to test advanced flight-control, maneuverability, and other cutting-edge technologies in real flight," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in the statement. The NASA chief called the aircraft "just one part of this new beginning for aeronautics" and said that the agency expects the X-70 to make its first flight within two years. "This is why people come to NASA: to build, to learn, and most importantly, to fly," Isaacman added. NASA's statement fleshes out a few details about the X-70's capabilities. According to the agency, Fractal will fly at a cruise speed of Mach .75, about the same as a Boeing 737 Classic. The X-70 will be able to reach altitudes of up to 45,000 feet (13.7 kilometers), and will have a range exceeding 1,726 miles (2,777 kilometers, or 1,500 nautical miles). The X-70 Fractal will also be able to carry around 2,000 pounds (900 kg) of experimental payloads both internally and externally, which will allow for a "wide range of research and flight-testing opportunities," NASA said in the statement. NASA adds it will have a takeoff weight of 10,000 pounds (4,535 kilograms), around the same weight as the Scaled Composites- and Northrop Grumman-developed Model 437 Vanguard experimental aircraft. In fact, the two aircraft share a similar silhouette — at least in the AI image of the X-70 Fractal NASA has released so far. Scaled Composites' Model 437 Vanguard experimental aircraft (top); NASA's render of its upcoming X-70 Fractal (bottom). (Image credit: Northrop Grumman/NASA) The agency's most recent X-plane, the X-59 , has been flying for over a year. That jet features a radical long-nosed geometry without a forward windscreen; pilots fly by way of an augmented reality screen that combines views from sensors and a forward-facing camera. That geometry dampens the shockwaves coming off of the X-59 when it flies faster than the sound barrier, allowing it to fly at speeds over Mach 1 without the thunderous sonic booms that typically accompany supersonic flight. item.title: 'Stop dirty datacenters': Europe-wide protests planned demanding building moratorium
item.description: Campaigners against datacenter expansion are planning two days of coordinated action across Europe on November 6 and 7, demanding an immediate moratorium on new large-scale developments. Following the US midterm elections , where restrictions on massive AI server farms were prominent in the campaigns from candidates in both major parties, it's now Europe's turn. Over 100 groups across 15 European countries will protest the boom in bit barn building over the next couple of days. As well as demonstrations, there will be public meetings, stalls, petitions, walking tours, cycle rides, poetry readings and other creative actions, the organizers say. The coalition of groups has put up a website – stopdirtydatacentres.eu – with an interactive map allowing anyone to find information on the events taking place and where. In the UK, there is a photocall planned at 8am on November 6 outside the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) in Whitehall Place in central London, but also a Community Day of Action the following day at London's Brick Lane, where a facility is planned on the site of the former Truman Brewery. Also on November 7, there will be a "family event" at St Michaels & All Angels Church in Great Torrington, Devon, to highlight the massive 1.5 GW data campus and on-site battery energy storage that is planned for 850 acres of farmland near the town. The planned actions are a response to growing concerns about the impact of the wave of new compute shed projects on local communities, public infrastructure, land, water and energy use, housing, jobs and the cost of living. Such concerns won't have been helped by recent events, such as a Google subsidiary reportedly felling 250,000 trees illegally in Finland to clear the ground for a server hall. The campaigners claim that governments, the European Union and the tech giants are gambling with the future by racing ahead with server farm developments without proper scrutiny of the environmental, democratic and social impacts they might have. A recent report found that businesses and private-sector trade associations dominated meetings with UK ministers to discuss datacenters, while environmental groups didn't get a look-in. Campaigners are calling for an immediate moratorium on new large-scale projects across Europe, until clear frameworks are in place to determine whether new facilities should be built and under what conditions, with proper scrutiny and meaningful public participation. "Datacenter developers in the UK and Europe want to cash in on the AI goldrush whatever the consequences. But communities everywhere are fighting back, seeing through Big Tech's PR machine and calling this what it is – a massive grab of scarce land, water and power resources by Silicon Valley billionaires," said Oliver Hayes, Head of Campaigns at Global Action Plan (UK). "With governments failing to answer very basic questions about how many datacenters we need, what for, where, and how pollution will be avoide

item.title: ‘Justice well served’, Keyamo lauds court ruling against Atiku, ADC
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr Festus Keyamo, SAN, has welcomed Thursday’s Federal High Court judgment that sacked the Senator David Mark-led leadership of the African Democratic Congress ADC, declaring that “justice may be slow, but it is always sure!” In the judgment delivered on Thursday, Justice Peter Lifu declared the Mark-led Caretaker Committee as illegal and invalidated all actions taken on its behalf. These included the nomination of a former vice president, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, as the ADC’s presidential candidate for the 2027 general election. Reacting to the outcome, Keyamo said the manner in which the party was taken over could not stand. “You cannot invade a political party owned and built by Nigerians and hijack it with the connivance of a so-called National Chairman without a prior meeting and approval of a mini National Convention or the National Executive Committee,” he said. The minister added that those behind the takeover could not “bluff your way out of such a brazen act by blaming and blackmailing the ruling Party for a misfortune deliberately stocked by you.” The judgment followed a suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, filed by the party’s former National Deputy Chairman (North-East), Nafiu Bala Gombe. He asked the court to nullify all actions taken by the Mark-led leadership, arguing that following the resignation of the former National Chairman, Chief Ralph Nwosu, he was qualified to take over the leadership of the party. The defendants were the ADC, the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Senator Mark, Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola and Chief Nwosu. Gombe also asked the court to stop Senator Mark and Aregbesola from presenting themselves as National Chairman and National Secretary, respectively, insisting that their emergence violated the party’s constitution and the Electoral Act. Justice Lifu upheld the plaintiff’s claims and granted his reliefs. Keyamo insisted that the court acted on the law and not on public feeling. “Sorry, but the law is decided on facts and evidence, rather than sentiments and outrage by a group of people,” he said. The ruling came barely 24 hours after Atiku held a rally in Sokoto State as part of his campaign for the January 16, 2027 presidential election. INEC had earlier published his name as a presidential candidate, and he has since picked a former Governor of Rivers State, Mr Rotimi Amaechi, as his running mate. The ADC has said it will challenge the judgment at the Court of Appeal. The party’s National Welfare Secretary, Mr Nkemakolam Ukandu, who was joined in the suit as an interested party, announced the decision to appeal. Keyamo, however, dismissed the notion that the judgment endangers democracy. “It is not only when a certain Atiku Abubakar contests the presidency that democracy is not in danger. The ADC as a party is well and alive and populated by people and original leaders who are no less Nigerians than David Mark and his illegal

item.title: NSCDC Smashes Border Gang Hideout In Ebonyi
item.description: Operatives of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Ebonyi State Command, have dismantled a criminal syndicate operating along the Ebonyi-Benue border, recovering an AK-47 rifle, live ammunition, and various dangerous items during a targeted sting operation. The operation, which targeted hideouts used by hoodlums and cult groups operating between Izzi Local Government Area in Ebonyi and neighboring Benue State, followed a week-long intelligence-gathering exercise. The raid was jointly executed by operatives from the Command’s Intelligence and Investigation Department alongside the State Commandant’s Special Squad. Briefing newsmen on Thursday at the Command Headquarters in Abakaliki, the State Commandant, Francis Nnadi, confirmed the success of the multi-location operation, highlighting the professional conduct of the officers during the raid on the fleeing suspects and their collaborators. During the sweep of the enclave, security operatives recovered the following items: 1 AK-47 rifle, 1 double-loaded magazine, 4 rounds of live ammunition, 1 locally-made pistol, 1 pump-action gun, 5 tactical knives, and assorted criminal charms. Issuing a strong warning to criminal networks operating within the state, Commandant Nnadi emphasized that the Command, in close synergy with sister security agencies, remains steadfast in wiping out criminality across Ebonyi. “I want to warn criminal elements ahead of the general elections to flee Ebonyi State. The Command, in conjunction with other sister security agencies, is fully prepared to rid the state of all forms of crime and criminality,” Nnadi stated. He further reassured residents in border areas and across the state of robust security coverage throughout the electoral season. “I want to assure residents of the border communities and the entire state of adequate security before, during, and after the elections.” “I urge the public to continue providing credible, timely information to assist security agencies in maintaining law and order,” he added. Manhunt operations are currently underway to track down and apprehend the fleeing suspects. The post NSCDC Smashes Border Gang Hideout In Ebonyi appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: ADC Rejects Judgment Voiding Atiku’s Candidacy, Accuses APC Of Desperation To Cripple Opposition
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has rejected the judgment by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, which sacked the Senator David Mark-led ADC leadership and invalidated the candidacy of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar. The party described the judgment as another desperate attempt by the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to cripple the opposition and deny Nigerians the right to choose their leaders in the forthcoming 2027 general elections. It added that the November 4 presidential campaign rally in Sokoto State sent the APC into panic. In a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, on Thursday, the party said the timing of the judgment, barely 24 hours after the massive turnout at the ADC presidential campaign rally in Sokoto, exposed what it considers the growing desperation of the APC. “We have reasons to believe that the judgment had long been written on this case. The Sokoto rally was simply a trigger that stampeded its delivery,” it stated. “Yesterday, Nigerians came out in their hundreds of thousands to demonstrate their support for the ADC and our promise of making life affordable for them. Today, they are being told that the party that they support and the candidates that they have supported at all levels could be erased by the stroke of a reckless judicial pen.” The opposition party questioned “whether those behind the flawed judgment” had considered its far-reaching implications for the country. It warned that the attempt to invalidate the party’s leadership could affect thousands of candidates contesting elections at the local, state and federal levels. “Do these people understand what they are playing with? This is not about Atiku Abubakar or David Mark. It is about the democratic rights of Nigerians to freely choose their own leaders. It is about the rights of thousands of candidates to participate in a democratic process,” it added. The ADC maintained that the judgment was legally indefensible and would be challenged through every available judicial process. “Our objection is particularly anchored on the subsisting judgment of Justice Musa Liman of the same Federal High Court, delivered on 2 July 2026 in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025, which affirmed the legitimacy of the David Mark-led NWC and directed INEC to recognise the leadership. It is a settled principle of Nigerian jurisprudence that a court of coordinate jurisdiction cannot sit on appeal over, review, vary or nullify the subsisting judgment of another court of equal jurisdiction,” it said. “The ADC, therefore, rejects any consequential orders founded on a determination that appears to disregard these fundamental legal principles. However, we await the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the said judgment to ascertain its precise terms, scope and operative orders.” Atiku (centre) is the presidential candidate of the ADC for the 2027 general elections.
